evidence.snippet: hALG2 was shown to act as an alpha1,3-mannosyltransferase.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the enzymatic identity of the deficient protein.

evidence.snippet: Western blot in whole cell lysates of HEK293 cells transfected with p.Gly80Asp, or p.Gly347Valfs*27 expression constructs indicated that p.Gly347Valfs*27 is likely a null allele and p.Gly80Asp is pathogenic through marked reduction of ALG2 expression.
evidence.explanation: Shows the mechanism of two alleles is reduced protein abundance, not altered kinetics of a normally expressed enzyme.

evidence.snippet: mutant ALG2 consistently shows a reduced Alg2 protein expression and lower glycan levels compared to wild-type controls
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation of the reduced-abundance mechanism for a third allele, p.Arg251Leu.

steps/1.description: Biallelic ALG2 variants reduce the abundance or catalytic activity of the ER membrane enzyme that adds both the alpha-1,3- and the alpha-1,6-mannose to Man1GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol. Reported alleles act by destabilising the protein rather than by abolishing catalysis on an otherwise normal enzyme: both the p.Gly80Asp missense and the p.Gly347Valfs*27 frameshift were shown to work through markedly reduced ALG2 expression, and the p.Arg251Leu homozygous allele likewise lowers protein level in a cell model.

evidence.snippet: An accumulation of Man1GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol and Man2GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol was observed in skin fibroblasts of the patient.
evidence.explanation: The accumulating intermediates locate the block precisely at the ALG2 step.

evidence.snippet: Alg2 mannosyltransferase adds both the α1,3- and α1,6-mannose (Man) onto ManGlcNAc2-pyrophosphate-dolichol (M1Gn2-PDol) in either order to generate the branched M3Gn2-PDol product.
evidence.explanation: Defines the reaction whose loss produces the accumulating intermediates, and shows the enzyme is bifunctional so one lesion removes two steps.

steps/2.description: ALG2 makes the first branch of the lipid-linked oligosaccharide, adding both the alpha-1,3- and alpha-1,6-mannose to Man1GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol to give the branched Man3GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol. When it is deficient the pathway backs up at the immediately preceding species: patient fibroblasts accumulate Man1GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol and Man2GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol instead of proceeding to the mature Glc3Man9GlcNAc2 donor.

evidence.snippet: Additional studies, including determination of carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT) revealed a mild type I CDG pattern and the presence of an abnormal transferrin glycoform containing a linear heptasaccharide consisting of one sialic acid, one galactose, one N-acetyl-glucosamine, two mannoses and two N-acetylglucosamines (NeuAc-Gal-GlcNAc-Man2-GlcNAc2), ALG2-CDG diagnostic biomarker, confirming the pathogenicity of these variants.
evidence.explanation: The heptasaccharide is the direct glycan-level readout of the stalled Man2 precursor being transferred to protein.

evidence.snippet: Molecularly, we detected reduced levels of N-glycans in medaka and in the patient's fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: The one sentence reports the measurement in both the fish and the index patient's own fibroblasts, so it supports hypoglycosylation in human cells as well. It is graded MODEL_ORGANISM because that is what the citing publication is, and the same sentence is graded identically where it is reused on the medaka model's readout.

steps/3.description: Sequons on secreted and membrane glycoproteins go unoccupied and the glycans that are transferred are immature, giving a type I CDG serum transferrin pattern. ALG2-CDG additionally produces a specific abnormal transferrin glycoform — a linear heptasaccharide NeuAc-Gal-GlcNAc-Man2-GlcNAc2 — which directly reflects transfer of the stalled Man2 precursor and is used as a diagnostic biomarker. Reduced overall N-glycan levels are measurable in patient fibroblasts.

evidence.snippet: We identify ALG14 and ALG2 as novel genes in which mutations cause a congenital myasthenic syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Establishes ALG2 as a neuromuscular junction disease gene.

evidence.snippet: Single fibre electromyography showed neuromuscular transmission failure and salbutamol and ephedrine treatment improved both muscle weakness and neuromuscular transmission.
evidence.explanation: Electrophysiological demonstration of transmission failure in an ALG2 patient, with pharmacological reversal.

steps/4.description: Hypoglycosylation at the motor endplate produces a failure of neuromuscular signal transmission. This is the mechanism of the CMS14 presentation, in which single-fibre electromyography shows transmission failure and the weakness is fatigable and limb-girdle in distribution rather than the generalised encephalopathy of the classic form.

evidence.snippet: Patients with ALG2-CDG have a multisystem disorder with mental disability, iris coloboma, hepatomegaly, coagulation abnormalities, and defective myelination
evidence.explanation: Summarises the human multisystem picture including the myelination defect. The quoted sentence is the paper's framing of the established human phenotype, not a result of its own cell-model experiments.

steps/5.description: The classic multisystem form is dominated by central nervous system disease: global developmental delay with regression, intractable seizures including infantile spasms, and hypomyelination on imaging. The medaka model of the index patient's allele shows reduced white matter in mid- and hindbrain, matching the human imaging finding.

evidence.snippet: These deficiencies relate to a specific failure to maintain rod photoreceptors, resulting in retinitis pigmentosa characterized by the progressive loss of these photoreceptors.
evidence.explanation: The model result. It is recorded as model-organism evidence because no equivalent human observation exists.

evidence.snippet: Proteins of the retinal phototransduction machinery, conversely, were massively under-represented in the alg2 model.
evidence.explanation: The proteomic mechanism proposed for the photoreceptor loss in the model.

steps/6.description:
An engineered model of the index patient's allele loses rod photoreceptors progressively, with the phototransduction machinery massively under-represented at the protein level, giving retinitis pigmentosa. No human ALG2-CDG patient has been reported with retinitis pigmentosa, so this node records a model finding whose translational status is open; it is flagged as a human/model mismatch rather than asserted as human disease biology. The eye features that are established in patients are developmental — iris coloboma and nystagmus — not degenerative.
This node is deliberately model-only: it has no inbound pathophysiology edge and no outbound edge to a human phenotype. An earlier version pointed it at Iris coloboma, which was wrong in the way this description already says it would be — coloboma is a failure of optic fissure closure during development, not a consequence of progressive rod loss. Wiring the node into the human chain in either direction would assert the translational claim the HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion exists to hold open.

evidence.snippet: The patient presented normal at birth but developed in the 1st year of life a multisystemic disorder with mental retardation, seizures, coloboma of the iris, hypomyelination, hepatomegaly, and coagulation abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: The index patient's hepatic and coagulation involvement, quoted in the full sentence that lists the founding case's multisystem features.

steps/7.description: Hepatomegaly and abnormal coagulation are recurrent extraneurological features. Coagulation factors and their regulators are N-glycoproteins synthesised in the liver, so their hypoglycosylation is the proximate cause of the coagulopathy; the same argument is standard across the type I CDGs. The finding is not universal in individual patients — the 2024 Mexican case had normal coagulation tests.

evidence.snippet: | Intellectual disability/global developmental delay | 10/14 | + | 11/15 |
evidence.explanation: The published denominator behind this frequency: 10 of 14 reported cases, which is FREQUENT and not VERY_FREQUENT.

evidence.snippet: Currently, it is recognized that ALG2-CDG exhibits a broad clinical spectrum, characterized primarily by global developmental delay and predominant muscular weakness.
evidence.explanation: Names global developmental delay as one of the two dominant features of the whole reported spectrum.

steps/8.description: Developmental delay with regression of acquired motor and mental milestones is the most consistent feature across both the classic and the myasthenic presentations.

evidence.explanation: The published denominator: 4 of 14 reported cases. This is the lowest of the three neurological features and was previously graded VERY_FREQUENT.

evidence.snippet: a multisystemic disorder with mental retardation, seizures, coloboma of the iris, hypomyelination, hepatomegaly, and coagulation abnormalities
evidence.explanation: Seizures in the index patient's multisystem presentation.

evidence.snippet: Pathogenic ALG2 variants lead to a severe multi-organ disease characterized by epilepsy, developmental delay, hypsarrhythmia, hepatomegaly, coagulation abnormalities, and ophthalmological manifestations
evidence.explanation: Names epilepsy and hypsarrhythmia in the disease summary. The quoted sentence is the paper's introduction restating the established human phenotype, not a result of its own fibroblast proteomics.

steps/9.description: Seizures begin in infancy and are often difficult to control, requiring multiple antiseizure medications. Hypsarrhythmia and infantile spasms are reported.

evidence.explanation: The published denominator: 9 of 14 reported cases. Note the table counts hypotonia generally, while this entry curates axial hypotonia specifically, so the figure bounds the broader feature.

evidence.snippet: We present the case of a baby who immediately after birth presented with pronounced truncal hypotonia, proximal muscle weakness and feeding difficulties.
evidence.explanation: Truncal hypotonia as the presenting sign.

evidence.snippet: axial hypotonia, and mental and motor regression
evidence.explanation: Axial hypotonia in the three-patient Argentinean series.

steps/10.description: Truncal and axial hypotonia is present from early infancy and is often the presenting sign, with depressed tendon reflexes.

evidence.snippet: We performed linkage analysis, whole-exome and whole-genome sequencing to determine the underlying defect in patients with an inherited limb-girdle pattern of myasthenic weakness.
evidence.explanation: The ascertainment phenotype of the kindreds in which ALG2 was identified as a congenital myasthenic syndrome gene.

steps/11.description: In the myasthenic presentation the weakness is limb-girdle in distribution and fatigable, with a decrement on repetitive stimulation and transmission failure on single-fibre electromyography. This is what distinguishes CMS14 from the generalised weakness of the encephalopathic form.

evidence.snippet: Dysmorphic features include a prominent forehead, metopic prominence, fan-shaped eyebrows, long eyelashes, sunken eyes, nystagmus, wide nasal bridge, full cheeks, thick nasal tip, prominent upper lip, high palate, retrognathia, pointed ears with hypoplastic helix and prominent concha
evidence.explanation: Documents nystagmus in the index patient. Note the source lists it among dysmorphic features rather than as an isolated ocular sign.

evidence.snippet: | Ocular symptoms (coloboma, strabismus, nystagmus and not specified) | 2/14 | + | 3/15 |
evidence.explanation: The only published denominator covering nystagmus, and it pools three distinct ocular signs, which is why no frequency is set on this phenotype.

steps/12.description: Nystagmus is recorded among the index patient's findings and is named in the ophthalmological features of the disorder. It is grouped with coloboma and strabismus in the one ocular row of the published feature table, so no nystagmus-specific denominator exists and none is asserted here.

evidence.snippet: The patient presented normal at birth but developed in the 1st year of life a multisystemic disorder with mental retardation, seizures, coloboma of the iris, hypomyelination, hepatomegaly, and coagulation abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Iris coloboma in the index patient, within the sentence listing the full presentation.

steps/13.description: Coloboma of the iris was present in the index patient and is listed among the recurrent ophthalmological features of the disorder.

evidence.snippet: The patient presented normal at birth but developed in the 1st year of life a multisystemic disorder with mental retardation, seizures, coloboma of the iris, hypomyelination, hepatomegaly, and coagulation abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Hypomyelination in the index patient, within the sentence listing the full presentation.

steps/14.description: Delayed or deficient myelination was described in the index patient and is part of the recognised neuroimaging picture.

evidence.snippet: The patient presented normal at birth but developed in the 1st year of life a multisystemic disorder with mental retardation, seizures, coloboma of the iris, hypomyelination, hepatomegaly, and coagulation abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Hepatomegaly in the index patient, within the sentence listing the full presentation.

evidence.snippet: The patient presented normal at birth but developed in the 1st year of life a multisystemic disorder with mental retardation, seizures, coloboma of the iris, hypomyelination, hepatomegaly, and coagulation abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Coagulation abnormality in the index patient, within the sentence listing the full presentation.

steps/16.description: Coagulation abnormalities are recurrent but not universal; the 2024 Mexican patient had normal coagulation tests, so a normal screen does not exclude the diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: Incubation of patient fibroblast extracts with Man1GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol and GDP-mannose revealed a severely reduced activity of the mannosyltransferase elongating Man1GlcNAc2-PP dolichol.
evidence.explanation: Direct enzymological demonstration in patient cells that the deficient step is the elongation of the dolichol-linked precursor.

edges/1.description: Losing the branching mannosyltransferase stops precursor elongation at the point where ALG2 acts.

evidence.snippet: Comparing it to control samples, we have observed Tf under-occupancy of glycosylation site(s) typical of a defective N-glycan assembly and the occurrence of oligomannose and hybrid type N-glycans.
evidence.explanation: Links the assembly defect to site under-occupancy on a specific serum glycoprotein in patients.

edges/2.description: A truncated lipid-linked oligosaccharide is a poor donor for the oligosaccharyltransferase, so glycosylation sequons go unoccupied.

evidence.snippet: Identification of DPAGT1, ALG14 and ALG2 mutations as a cause of congenital myasthenic syndrome underscores the importance of asparagine-linked protein glycosylation for proper functioning of the neuromuscular junction.
evidence.explanation: States the causal relationship between the N-glycosylation defect and neuromuscular junction failure.

edges/3.description: Acetylcholine receptor subunits and other endplate proteins are N-glycosylated, and glycosylation defects at this step impair neuromuscular transmission.

edges/4.description: Hypoglycosylation of neuronal glycoproteins underlies the encephalopathy, hypomyelination and seizures of the multisystem form.

edges/5.description: Coagulation factors and their inhibitors are N-glycoproteins, so their hypoglycosylation is the proximate cause of the coagulopathy.

edges/6.description: Coloboma is a failure of optic fissure closure in the embryo, so it is placed on the developmental branch of hypoglycosylation rather than downstream of photoreceptor maintenance. Which glycoprotein's hypoglycosylation causes the fissure to stay open is not known, hence unknown intermediates.

edges/7.description: Grouped with coloboma on the developmental branch for the same reason. The source that quantifies the eye findings counts coloboma, strabismus and nystagmus together as one ocular category, so no route separating them is available.

evidence.snippet: Mutations were identified in two kinships, with mutation ALG2p.Val68Gly found to severely reduce ALG2 expression both in patient muscle, and in cell cultures.
evidence.explanation: Gene-disease evidence for the myasthenic presentation, with the functional consequence measured in patient tissue.

evidence.snippet: Expression of wild type but not of mutant hALG2 cDNA restored the mannosyltransferase activity and the biosynthesis of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides both in patient fibroblasts and in the alg2-1 yeast cells.
evidence.explanation: Complementation establishing that the ALG2 variants, and not another locus, cause the biochemical defect.

genes/0.notes: ALG2 (9q31.1) encodes the ER alpha-1,3/1,6-mannosyltransferase. Every published ALG2-CDG genotype is biallelic. The functionally characterised alleles act by lowering protein abundance rather than by producing a normally-expressed but catalytically dead enzyme, which fits the observation that complete loss of ALG2 is expected to be lethal and that surviving patients carry hypomorphic combinations.

evidence.snippet: Our findings suggest that treatment with cholinesterase inhibitors may improve muscle function in many of the congenital disorders of glycosylation.
evidence.explanation: The authors' therapeutic inference from identifying ALG2 as a CMS gene. It is a suggestion about a class of disorders, not a trial result in ALG2 patients, hence INDIRECT.

evidence.snippet: From a pharmacological point of view, cholinesterase inhibitors are effective in most groups of CMS, but are contraindicated in some groups of CMS.
evidence.explanation: The class-level statement, including the contraindication warning that makes genotype-before-treatment the rule here. A review's synthesis across 35 genes, not an ALG2 result.

treatments/0.description: Pyridostigmine and other cholinesterase inhibitors are the first-line pharmacological approach in the myasthenic presentation. The evidence is class-level rather than ALG2-specific: cholinesterase inhibitors help in most congenital myasthenic syndrome groups and are contraindicated in some, so the genetic subtype must be known before starting.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Prolongs acetylcholine dwell time in the synaptic cleft, compensating for a reduced safety margin of transmission rather than correcting the glycosylation defect.

evidence.snippet: Single fibre electromyography showed neuromuscular transmission failure and salbutamol and ephedrine treatment improved both muscle weakness and neuromuscular transmission.
evidence.explanation: A single-patient response, the only ALG2-specific treatment datum.

treatments/1.description: Salbutamol (albuterol) and ephedrine improved both weakness and measured neuromuscular transmission in a genetically confirmed ALG2 infant. This is the one treatment claim in this entry supported by an observation in an ALG2 patient rather than by extrapolation from the congenital myasthenic syndrome class.

evidence.snippet: salbutamol and ephedrine treatment improved both muscle weakness and neuromuscular transmission
evidence.explanation: Response measured electrophysiologically as well as clinically, which is what makes it evidence about the endplate node specifically.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Both agents are used in congenital myasthenic syndromes to improve endplate function; the mechanism at the endplate is not established for either.

treatments/2.description: Antiseizure medication for the epilepsy, gastrostomy for feeding failure, respiratory surveillance, and monitoring of coagulation and liver function. No disease-modifying therapy exists.

open_questions/0.rationale: The medaka model built from the index patient's allele develops retinitis pigmentosa with massively under-represented phototransduction proteins, and the authors present it as a central result. Human ALG2-CDG eye disease, by contrast, is reported as developmental — iris coloboma, nystagmus — with no published case of retinitis pigmentosa. The disagreement has at least three possible resolutions and nothing currently separates them: the fish dies 2-3 days after hatching so the human timescale may simply be longer than anyone has looked; teleost and mammalian photoreceptor maintenance differ; or the human patients with the most severe alleles die or are too neurologically impaired for the retinal examination that would find it. This matters clinically, because if the first explanation is right then surviving ALG2-CDG patients need retinal surveillance nobody currently performs.

open_questions/1.rationale: The same gene and the same biochemical lesion give two clinical pictures that a clinician would not group together: intractable infantile epilepsy with coloboma, hypomyelination and coagulopathy on one side, and fatigable limb-girdle weakness responsive to salbutamol on the other. The obvious hypothesis is residual enzyme activity — more residual activity spares the brain and leaves only the endplate, which has the least safety margin. But the characterised alleles on both sides act by reducing protein abundance, and nobody has measured residual mannosyltransferase activity across enough genotypes to test a dose-response. With fourteen patients worldwide, the cohort may never be large enough, which is an argument for a cell-based activity assay rather than for waiting.

evidence.snippet: We found multiple loss-of-function mutations in ARX in individuals affected with XLAG and in some female relatives, and conclude that mutation of ARX causes XLAG.
evidence.explanation: Establishes pathogenic ARX loss of function as the cause of human XLAG.

evidence.snippet: We show that the most likely, common pathogenic mechanism of the missense mutations in NLS regions of the ARX homeodomain is inadequate accumulation and distribution of the ARX transcription factor within the nucleus due to sequestration of ARX with IPO13.
evidence.explanation: Severe homeodomain variants can create functional ARX deficiency by disrupting nuclear localization rather than by eliminating the protein.

steps/1.description: Complete loss-of-function and severe homeodomain variants reduce or mislocalize functional nuclear ARX. This is the initiating molecular lesion in classic XLAG; hypomorphic and polyalanine-expansion alleles can produce different ARX-related disorders and are not assumed to follow every branch modeled here.

evidence.snippet: Aristaless-related homeobox (ARX) is a paired-like homeodomain transcription factor that functions primarily as a transcriptional repressor and has been implicated in neocortical interneuron specification and migration.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the transcription-factor role that connects ARX deficiency to interneuron developmental programs.

evidence.snippet: Single-cell RNA sequencing combined with chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-seq revealed ARX regulates key processes involved in cell cycle progression, cIN subtype differentiation, guidance cues and receptors, as well as other transcription factors.
evidence.explanation: Integrated transcriptional and chromatin evidence identifies the affected cortical-interneuron developmental programs.

steps/2.description: ARX deficiency perturbs transcriptional programs governing forebrain progenitor proliferation, cortical-interneuron lineage differentiation and guidance, basal-ganglia and thalamocortical development, and testicular differentiation. ARX can regulate targets through context-dependent repression or derepression, so this node does not assume a single direction for every target gene.

evidence.snippet: In these animals, the early differentiation of this tissue appeared normal, whereas subsequent differentiation was impaired, leading to the periventricular accumulation of immature neurons in both the lateral ganglionic eminence and medial ganglionic eminence (MGE).
evidence.explanation: Defines the post-patterning lineage defect in Arx-mutant ganglionic eminences.

evidence.snippet: In these mice, we observed defects in cell cycle exit, a biased loss of the marginal zone migration stream of cINs, shifts in cell fate from caudal ganglionic eminence (CGE) to medial ganglionic eminence (MGE) identity, and a reduced number of parvalbumin⁺ and somatostatin⁺ cINs, with parvalbumin⁺ cINs being more severely affected.
evidence.explanation: Current conditional-model evidence resolves multiple components of the disrupted lineage program.

steps/3.description: ARX-dependent programs in the ganglionic eminences regulate cortical-interneuron cell-cycle exit, subtype identity, differentiation, and guidance. Their disruption is the conserved upstream interneuronopathy branch of XLAG.

evidence.snippet: In these animals, the early differentiation of this tissue appeared normal, whereas subsequent differentiation was impaired, leading to the periventricular accumulation of immature neurons in both the lateral ganglionic eminence and medial ganglionic eminence (MGE).
evidence.explanation: Shows later differentiation failure and immature-neuron accumulation.

evidence.snippet: instead of a loss of ventral precursors, there is a shift of these precursors to more ventral locations
evidence.explanation: Corrects a simple precursor-loss interpretation by showing ventral mispositioning.

steps/4.description: ARX-deficient ventral precursors are mispositioned and fail to complete normal later differentiation, accumulating as immature neurons in ganglionic-eminence regions. The evidence does not support simple depletion of the initial precursor pool.

evidence.snippet: Both tangential migration toward the cortex and striatum and radial migration to the globus pallidus and striatum were greatly reduced in the mutants, causing a periventricular accumulation of NPY+ or calretinin+ neurons in the MGE.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates reduced tangential migration in Arx-mutant mice.

evidence.snippet: Our findings suggest that ARX protein controls not only the tangential migration of GABAergic interneurons from the ganglionic eminence, but also may serve to induce radial migration from the neocortical subventricular zone.
evidence.explanation: Human XLAG neuropathology supports ARX-dependent interneuron migration.

evidence.snippet: X-linked lissencephaly with abnormal genitalia is the first human disorder in which deficient tangential migration in the brain has been demonstrated.
evidence.explanation: Frames XLAG as the human prototype of deficient tangential migration.

evidence.snippet: Cortical slice cultures demonstrate that LMO1 inhibits cIN migration by repressing Cxcr4 expression, which encodes a key receptor involved in cortical guidance.
evidence.explanation: Mouse cortical-slice experiments provide a current ARX-target/guidance mechanism for the migration branch.

steps/5.description: ARX-deficient cortical-interneuron precursors show reduced tangential migration from medial and lateral ganglionic eminences toward the neocortex. This is a well-supported conserved branch, but it is not treated as a proven sufficient cause of the human gyral malformation.

open_questions/0.rationale: Mouse models validate the conserved subpallial interneuronopathy and several ARX-specific developmental branches. They do not establish that tangential interneuron migration failure is sufficient for human lissencephaly. Human XLAG neuropathology suggests an additional radial-migration contribution from the neocortical subventricular zone, while general human lissencephaly work shows that outer radial glia important for neocortical expansion are largely absent from lissencephalic rodents. The canonical graph therefore does not connect tangential migration directly to lissencephaly; an explicitly alternative, human-enriched dorsal cortical route carries that endpoint.

steps/1.description: Nearly all individuals have one of two substitutions producing p.Gly380Arg. The receptor is gain of function, but experiments show predominantly ligand-dependent activation with delayed down-regulation and resistance to ligand-mediated internalization.

evidence.snippet: transgenic mice expressing the human G380R mutant receptor under the mouse receptor transcriptional control demonstrated a markedly expanded area of FGFR3 immunoreactivity within their epiphyseal growth plates, compatible with an in vivo defect in receptor down-regulation.
evidence.explanation: Transgenic mice provide in vivo evidence for expanded receptor persistence.

steps/2.description: Delayed internalization expands mutant FGFR3 immunoreactivity in epiphyseal growth plates, where signal kinetics regulate chondrocyte maturation.

evidence.snippet: Here we showed that in chondrocytes from human (ACH, TD) and mouse Fgfr3Y367C/+ cartilage, the constitutively active FGFR3 perturbed PC length and the sorting and trafficking of intraflagellar transport (IFT) 20 to the PC.
evidence.explanation: Chondrocytes taken from human achondroplasia and thanatophoric dysplasia cartilage, alongside a mouse model, show the ciliary length and IFT20 trafficking defect.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report in vivo evidence for significantly shortened primary cilia in ACH and TD cartilage growth plates.
evidence.explanation: Supplies the in vivo growth-plate measurement of cilium shortening. The achondroplasia arm of this experiment is an Fgfr3 p.Gly369Cys mouse and the thanatophoric arm is a transfected cell line, so it is graded as model-organism evidence despite the title's ciliopathy framing.

steps/3.description: Sustained FGFR3 activity shortens the chondrocyte primary cilium and disrupts sorting and intraflagellar transport of IFT20, with downstream change in cilium-based Hedgehog signaling. This branch is curated as an emerging consequence of receptor activation, not as an independent cause: its quantitative contribution relative to the direct MAPK and STAT arms has not been isolated in human growth plate, and the entry does not classify achondroplasia as a ciliopathy on this evidence.

evidence.snippet: These observations indicate that the MAPK pathway inhibits hypertrophic differentiation of chondrocytes and negatively regulates bone growth without inhibiting chondrocyte proliferation.
evidence.explanation: Active MEK1 supports inhibition of hypertrophic differentiation by MAPK.

evidence.snippet: Immunohistochemical analysis of fetal growth plates showed a phenotype-related reduction of the collagen type X-positive hypertrophic zone.
evidence.explanation: Human fetal histology documents a reduced hypertrophic zone.

steps/4.description: MAPK inhibits hypertrophic differentiation in models. Human fetal growth plates support altered FGFR3/STAT/p21 expression and premature cell-cycle exit. STAT1 is not treated as sufficient to explain all growth inhibition.

evidence.snippet: This mutation leads to impaired endochondral ossification of the human skeleton.
evidence.explanation: International consensus identifies the central consequence.

steps/5.description: Altered growth-plate maturation reduces the hypertrophic zone and impairs endochondral ossification. Anatomical consequences are represented through calibrated branches rather than an unsupported all-phenotype fan-out.

evidence.snippet: Chondrocyte-specific activation of Fgfr3 in mice induced premature synchondrosis closure and enhanced osteoblast differentiation around synchondroses.
evidence.explanation: Chondrocyte-specific activation establishes a causal model mechanism.

evidence.snippet: All patients with available CT-scan had premature fusion of skull base synchondroses.
evidence.explanation: CT documents skull-base fusion in a clinical cohort.

steps/6.description: FGFR3-MAPK activation promotes premature closure in models and severe human FGFR3 dysplasias. CT in heterozygous achondroplasia documents skull-base fusion and age-associated craniofacial severity.

evidence.snippet: CNP prevented the shortening of achondroplastic bones by correcting the decreased extracellular matrix synthesis in the growth plate through inhibition of the MAPK pathway of FGF signaling.
evidence.explanation: Mouse data support CNP counter-regulation of MAPK.

evidence.snippet: CNP had no effect on the STAT-1 pathway of FGF signaling that mediates the decreased proliferation and the delayed differentiation of achondroplastic chondrocytes.
evidence.explanation: The model defines the limitation on the STAT1 branch.

steps/7.description: CNP signaling through NPR2/GC-B counteracts FGFR3-MAPK activity. CNP corrected matrix synthesis and bone shortening in a mouse model without correcting the STAT1 branch.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with achondroplasia have short stature with rhizomelic shortening of the limbs, macrocephaly, characteristic facies with frontal bossing and midface retrusion, exaggerated lumbar lordosis, limitation of elbow extension and rotation, genu varum, brachydactyly, and trident appearance of the hands.
evidence.explanation: The current review documents the characteristic pattern.

steps/8.description: Reduced long-bone growth produces disproportionate short stature, rhizomelic limb shortening, and characteristic hand shortening.

evidence.snippet: This condition causes a partial obstruction of venous flow, which increases intracranial venous pressure and causes problems with the venous resorption of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)
evidence.explanation: The study states the venous and CSF-resorption mechanism.

steps/9.description: Narrow jugular foramina can obstruct cerebral venous drainage, increasing venous pressure and impairing cerebrospinal-fluid resorption.

evidence.snippet: We report a significant correlation between the severity of maxillo-mandibular retrusion and obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (p < 0.01).
evidence.explanation: Clinical morphometry links retrusion with obstructive sleep apnea.

steps/10.description: Midface and maxillomandibular retrusion reduce upper-airway dimensions; lymphoid hypertrophy, airway malacia, and hypotonia can add obstruction. evidence.snippet: Unlike the general population, spinal stenosis and disc degeneration involve the upper part of the lumbar spine in adults with achondroplasia, associated with thoraco-lumbar kyphosis and loss of lumbar lordosis.
evidence.explanation: Adult imaging supports combined stenotic and degenerative components.

steps/11.description: Altered vertebral geometry constrains the canal; disc degeneration and sagittal deformity add to adult upper-lumbar narrowing.

evidence.snippet: the size of the cranial base, which is formed by endochondral ossification, is smaller, and the jugular foramen is also smaller. evidence.explanation: Describes the mechanistic basis of communicating hydrocephalus in achondroplasia—endochondral hypoplasia of the skull base narrows the jugular foramina, causing venous outflow obstruction, intracranial venous hypertension, and impaired CSF resorption.

steps/25.description: Hydrocephalus is a rare but clinically important neurosurgical complication in childhood. It is typically communicating and attributed to endochondral hypoplasia of the skull base, which narrows the jugular foramina and obstructs cerebral venous outflow, raising intracranial venous pressure and impairing CSF resorption.

treatments/2.description: Once-daily oral ATP-competitive FGFR1-3 tyrosine kinase inhibitor, repurposed from oncology at roughly a hundredth of the oncology dose (0.25 mg/kg/day). open_questions/0.rationale: These features are well documented, but the cited sources provide descriptive or association-level statements only. Proposed contributors include relative sparing of membranous calvarial growth against a restricted endochondral skull base, markedly delayed sutural closure, frontal-bone ossification delay (raised as a possibility in the craniofacial 3D study), and, for macrocephaly, brain and CSF-compartment factors related to venous outflow. open_questions/1.rationale: Hypotonia and generalized joint laxity are documented proximate contributors to motor delay and dynamic knee instability, and infantile thoracolumbar kyphosis is managed clinically as a consequence of truncal hypotonia during unsupported sitting, usually resolving as trunk strength increases and walking begins. No cited source establishes how FGFR3 gain of function produces the hypotonia or the ligamentous laxity (candidate contributors include craniocervical compression for hypotonia), so no causal edge is asserted for these phenotypes.

open_questions/2.rationale: Obesity begins in early childhood and is prevalent at all ages, and caloric needs are reduced, but no cited source establishes a mechanistic route from FGFR3 gain of function to the energy-balance phenotype. Wiring obesity through the skeletal growth-plate nodes would manufacture a causal claim, so the phenotype is deliberately left without a causal edge.

open_questions/3.rationale: Acanthosis nigricans recurs across the FGFR3-activating disorder family (SADDAN, thanatophoric dysplasia, Crouzon syndrome with acanthosis nigricans, familial acanthosis nigricans), suggesting direct receptor activation in skin. Direct evidence in ordinary heterozygous achondroplasia is not present in the cited sources, and the skeletal growth-plate nodes would be the wrong upstream route regardless, so the phenotype is left without a causal edge.

evidence.snippet: The CDK8 expression and STAT1Ser727 phosphorylation were upregulated in chondrocytes isolated from ACH model mice, and KY-065 repressed its phosphorylation and restored normal chondrogenic differentiation without affecting MAPK activation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the STAT1 arm is separately druggable in a mouse model without engaging MAPK, which is what makes the arm-attribution question experimentally answerable.

evidence.snippet: These results suggest that TACC3 might play a role through the p38 signaling pathway in chondrocyte differentiation defects caused by FGFR3 mutations.
evidence.explanation: The whole current basis for a p38 branch is this ATDC5 cell-line result, whose authors state it only as a suggestion; it is recorded here rather than curated as an established signaling arm.

open_questions/4.rationale: Mouse genetics separates the arms — CNP overexpression corrects matrix synthesis through MAPK without touching STAT1, constitutively active MEK1 causes Stat1-independent dwarfism — and a CDK8 inhibitor now moves the STAT1-Ser727 branch in a mouse model without affecting MAPK activation. No study has tested the two interventions together, and no human data assign specific clinical features to specific arms; the vosoritide result is consistent with the model but does not rank the arms against each other. A third, p38 branch is proposed on the strength of a single ATDC5 cell-line study and is not curated as a pathophysiology node here for that reason.

evidence.snippet: Transcriptomic analysis in an Fgfr3 mouse model showed that ciliary mRNA expression was modified and influenced significantly by the Indian hedgehog and PKA pathways.
evidence.explanation: Shows the ciliary program is transcriptionally entangled with hedgehog and PKA signaling in the model, which is why an intervention that restores ciliogenesis does not isolate a ciliary contribution.

open_questions/5.rationale: Cilium shortening and IFT20 mis-sorting are reproducible in chondrocytes from human achondroplasia and thanatophoric dysplasia cartilage and in mouse models, and a ciliogenesis-restoring compound increases bone elongation in the mouse. What has not been done is a measurement that separates the ciliary contribution from the receptor's direct signaling output: every available intervention acts upstream of both, and the rescue compound is not cilia-selective. Until such an experiment exists, the "achondroplasia is a ciliopathy" reading found in the source literature is an interpretive proposal rather than an established classification, and this entry curates the branch without adopting that label.

evidence.snippet: We conclude that statins do not inhibit the FGFR signaling in chondrocytes. Therefore the statin-mediated rescue of FGFR3-related chondrodysplasia, described before, is likely not intrinsic to the growth plate cartilage.
evidence.explanation: The authors state both halves of the gap: the chondrocyte-intrinsic FGFR mechanism is excluded, and the mechanism behind the earlier rescue is left open.

open_questions/6.rationale: A dedicated study found no effect of four statins on FGFR3 protein levels or on FGFR-mediated growth arrest, matrix loss, senescence, or hypertrophic differentiation across chondrocyte lines, embryonic tibia cultures, and limb-bud micromasses. That result narrows the earlier rescue reports: it rules out a chondrocyte-intrinsic FGFR mechanism, but it does not exclude an indirect or systemic effect, so statins are recorded here as an unresolved question rather than as a refuted therapy outright. No statin treatment entry is curated for this disease.

evidence.snippet: At the late stage of severe hemorrhage (equivalent to loss of approximately 30% of blood volume), a paradoxical increase of vagal drive may occur leading to a decrease in heart rate, and systemic vascular resistance resulting in a reduction of arterial blood pressure, and possibly to a circulatory collapse (26, 29, 30).
evidence.explanation: This physiologic discussion supports severe volume loss as one route to an acute arterial-pressure fall, while also showing that compensation varies with severity.

steps/0.description: Hemorrhage, external fluid loss, or redistribution of intravascular volume can reduce venous return, cardiac preload, and stroke volume. evidence.snippet: The initial compensatory mechanism is frequently a tachycardia often resulting in a near normal cardiac output. In more severe forms a fall in cardiac output causes hypotension or cardiogenic shock.

steps/1.description: Acute pump failure can reduce stroke volume and cardiac output. Tachycardia and vascular compensation may preserve pressure in milder states, but a sufficiently large output fall can cause hypotension or cardiogenic shock.

evidence.snippet: Vasoplegia is a condition characterized by persistent low systemic vascular resistance despite a normal or high cardiac index, resulting in profound and uncontrolled vasodilation.
evidence.explanation: This defines the low-resistance, vasodilatory mechanism independently of a low cardiac index.

steps/2.description: Loss of systemic vascular tone lowers the resistance component of arterial pressure. In vasoplegia, systemic vascular resistance remains low despite a normal or high cardiac index, producing profound vasodilation.

evidence.snippet: Categories include distributive, hypovolemic, obstructive, and cardiogenic, of which distributive (and usually septic distributive) shock is by far the most common.
evidence.explanation: The review establishes obstructive shock as a distinct category, but its abstract does not resolve every intervening mechanism linking obstruction to a pressure fall.

steps/3.description: Mechanical obstruction of cardiac filling or ejection is a distinct hemodynamic route to low forward flow. If compensation is insufficient, the resulting output limitation can contribute to an acute pressure fall; when organ perfusion is impaired, the clinical state is obstructive shock.

evidence.snippet: Although hypotension is common in acute care, there is a lack of accepted criteria for its definition.

steps/4.description: Diverse changes in circulating volume, cardiac output, and systemic vascular resistance converge on an abrupt fall in arterial pressure. evidence.snippet: We also propose a haemodynamic pyramid and a pressure-output-resistance triangle to facilitate understanding of why hypotension can have different pathophysiological mechanisms and end-organ effects.
evidence.explanation: This supports modeling heterogeneous end-organ effects as a distinct conditional mechanism rather than as an inevitable synonym for low pressure.

steps/5.description: Organ blood flow can fall when perfusion pressure decreases beyond the compensatory range set by regional vascular resistance and autoregulation. The same measured blood pressure can therefore have different end-organ effects in different patients and organs.

steps/7.description: Irreversible AMSAN injury is dominated by Wallerian-like degeneration and loss of motor and sensory fibers in ventral and dorsal roots and peripheral nerves. This acute pattern is not assumed to be length-dependent, and primary demyelination is not required.

evidence.snippet: axonal neuropathies are simply diagnosed by reduced amplitude of motor and sensory nerve action potentials with normal or slightly slow conduction velocity.
evidence.explanation: The conventional motor-amplitude pattern supports the finding, while the review and serial GBS data caution against over-simple subtype inference.

steps/8.description: Motor nerve conduction studies show reduced or absent compound muscle action potential amplitudes. Serial testing is needed because reversible conduction failure and fixed motor-axon loss can initially appear similar.

evidence.snippet: axonal neuropathies are simply diagnosed by reduced amplitude of motor and sensory nerve action potentials with normal or slightly slow conduction velocity.
evidence.explanation: Reduced sensory amplitudes are part of the conventional axonal pattern; AMSAN classification still requires clinical context and serial testing.

steps/9.description: Sensory nerve conduction studies show reduced or absent sensory nerve action potential amplitudes, distinguishing a motor-sensory pattern from motor-only AMAN when the finding is reproducible and not explained by another neuropathy.

evidence.snippet: progressive flaccid limb paresis and areflexia.
evidence.explanation: This is the hallmark motor-sensory GBS phenotype and therefore applies to AMSAN, without supplying an AMSAN-specific frequency.

steps/10.description: Acute, usually symmetric, progressive flaccid weakness affects the legs and arms and may progress to inability to walk or complete paralysis.

evidence.snippet: progressive flaccid limb paresis and areflexia.
evidence.explanation: Areflexia is a defining GBS-wide clinical feature relevant to AMSAN.

steps/11.description: Tendon reflexes are reduced or absent in affected limbs because the peripheral reflex arc is impaired.

evidence.snippet: axonal lesions of both motor and sensory fibers
evidence.explanation: Direct human AMSAN autopsy confirms sensory-fiber involvement, with the limitation of a small fatal-case series.

steps/12.description: Objective sensory loss and abnormal sensory responses reflect involvement of sensory roots and peripheral sensory axons.

evidence.snippet: weakness and paraesthesia in both her legs and arms for 4 days
evidence.explanation: A single AMSAN case illustrates paresthesia but does not establish its frequency.

steps/13.description: Tingling or other abnormal sensations can accompany weakness, often early in the illness.

evidence.snippet: Pain is a serious manifestation in both the acute and chronic stages of Guillain-Barre syndrome
evidence.explanation: This prospective GBS cohort supports pain and reports an association with axonal GBS, but does not give an AMSAN-specific rate.

steps/14.description: Radicular, neuropathic, and musculoskeletal pain can occur during the acute illness and may persist into recovery.

evidence.snippet: dysarthria, dysphagia, bilateral facial paralysis, facial diplegia
evidence.explanation: This case documents dysphagia during AMSAN progression; it is illustrative rather than frequency evidence.

steps/15.description: Bulbar and cranial motor involvement can impair swallowing and increase aspiration risk.

evidence.snippet: Around 20% of patients may develop weakness in all four limbs (tetraparesis) and respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
evidence.explanation: GBS-wide evidence supports the severe complication; no AMSAN-specific frequency is asserted.

steps/16.description: Severe motor weakness can involve respiratory muscles and require invasive ventilation even before prominent dyspnea is reported.

evidence.snippet: The most severely affected patients also develop ... autonomic dysfunction
evidence.explanation: The current GBS primer supports dysautonomia in severe disease; the applicability is GBS-wide rather than AMSAN-specific.

steps/17.description: Dysautonomia can manifest as heart-rate or blood-pressure instability, gastrointestinal dysmotility, or bladder dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: On sensitization with C. jejuni lipooligosaccharide, rabbits developed anti-GM1 IgG antibody
evidence.explanation: The intervention directly links bacterial LOS exposure to anti-GM1 IgG production in vivo.

edges/0.description: LOS-ganglioside mimicry elicits IgG that cross-reacts with neural gangliosides.

evidence.snippet: Dense antibody and complement deposits were observed only over presynaptic motor axons
evidence.explanation: The ex vivo model directly demonstrates antibody deposition on axonal membranes but models motor terminals rather than sensory-inclusive AMSAN.

edges/1.description: Circulating anti-ganglioside IgG binds ganglioside-rich vulnerable sites on peripheral axons and motor nerve terminals.

evidence.snippet: Dense antibody and complement deposits were observed only over presynaptic motor axons
evidence.explanation: Co-localized antibody and complement deposition directly supports the binding-to-complement edge in a motor-terminal preparation.

edges/2.description: Axon-bound IgG recruits C1q and initiates the classical complement pathway.

evidence.snippet: complement mediated dysfunction and disruption of the nodes of Ranvier which causes a pathophysiological continuum from early reversible conduction failure to axonal degeneration.
evidence.explanation: The review explicitly links complement-mediated nodal disruption to the reversible-conduction-failure end of the axonal GBS continuum.

edges/3.description: Complement-mediated nodal membrane dysfunction can block conduction before irreversible axonal loss occurs.

evidence.snippet: attenuated complement cascade activation and deposition, reduced immune cell recruitment and axonal injury
evidence.explanation: C1q blockade reduced both complement deposition and immune-cell recruitment, supporting an indirect complement-to-recruitment link in a motor-axonal model.

edges/4.description: Complement products promote recruitment of macrophages and other immune cells to injured neural membranes.

evidence.snippet: a pathophysiological continuum from early reversible conduction failure to axonal degeneration.
evidence.explanation: This synthesis explicitly places axonal degeneration downstream of the complement-mediated nodal process.

edges/5.description: Persistent complement-mediated membrane injury can cross the threshold from reversible dysfunction to irreversible axonal degeneration.

evidence.snippet: transient conduction block/slowing in intermediate and distal nerve segments
evidence.explanation: Conduction block provides a functional route to a reduced motor response; amplitude is not separately quantified in this review excerpt.

edges/6.description: Failure of motor-axon conduction reduces the evoked compound muscle action potential even when the axon has not yet degenerated.

evidence.snippet: axonal neuropathies are simply diagnosed by reduced amplitude of motor and sensory nerve action potentials with normal or slightly slow conduction velocity.
evidence.explanation: The review states the conventional axonal-amplitude heuristic while cautioning that electrophysiology-pathology relationships are more complex; serial GBS studies remain necessary.

edges/7.description: Loss of functioning motor axons reduces or abolishes compound muscle action potential amplitudes.

evidence.snippet: axonal neuropathies are simply diagnosed by reduced amplitude of motor and sensory nerve action potentials with normal or slightly slow conduction velocity.
evidence.explanation: The conventional amplitude pattern is relevant to AMSAN, but the review warns against treating it as a simple one-to-one pathology rule.

edges/8.description: Loss of functioning sensory axons reduces or abolishes sensory nerve action potential amplitudes.

evidence.snippet: flaccid limb weakness of acute onset
evidence.explanation: The rabbit model links acute axonal injury to flaccid weakness but does not reproduce the sensory component of AMSAN.

edges/9.description: Motor-axon loss reduces muscle activation and produces acute flaccid limb weakness.

evidence.snippet: progressive flaccid limb paresis and areflexia.
evidence.explanation: The motor-sensory GBS primer links peripheral nerve dysfunction with the hallmark weakness-areflexia phenotype; evidence is not AMSAN-frequency data.

edges/10.description: Failure of peripheral motor and sensory limbs of the reflex arc reduces or abolishes tendon reflexes.

evidence.snippet: axonal lesions of both motor and sensory fibers
evidence.explanation: Direct AMSAN autopsy evidence establishes sensory-fiber as well as motor-fiber injury.

edges/11.description: Dorsal-root and sensory-nerve axonal loss produces objective sensory dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: weakness and paraesthesia in both her legs and arms for 4 days
evidence.explanation: A single AMSAN case directly illustrates paresthesia but cannot establish frequency or mechanism by itself.

edges/12.description: Injured sensory fibers can generate tingling and other abnormal sensations.

evidence.snippet: Pain is a serious manifestation in both the acute and chronic stages of Guillain-Barre syndrome
evidence.explanation: The prospective cohort supports pain across GBS and reports association with axonal GBS, but does not isolate AMSAN.

edges/13.description: Sensory-fiber and root injury can produce neuropathic, radicular, and musculoskeletal pain.

evidence.snippet: dysarthria, dysphagia, bilateral facial paralysis, facial diplegia
evidence.explanation: This AMSAN case documents bulbar and cranial progression but is anecdotal and cannot define frequency.

edges/14.description: Severe cranial motor-nerve involvement can impair swallowing.

evidence.snippet: Around 20% of patients may develop weakness in all four limbs (tetraparesis) and respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
evidence.explanation: This is GBS-wide severe-disease evidence rather than an AMSAN-specific respiratory-risk estimate.

edges/15.description: Severe motor-axon dysfunction can weaken respiratory muscles and require ventilatory support.

evidence.snippet: The most severely affected patients also develop ... autonomic dysfunction
evidence.explanation: The primer supports autonomic dysfunction in severe GBS; the exact AMSAN frequency is unknown.

edges/16.description: Involvement of autonomic peripheral fibers can produce cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and bladder dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: patients with C. jejuni infection have anti-GM1 and anti-GD1a antibodies and are susceptible to developing motor and axonal forms of GBS
evidence.explanation: Connects the antecedent infection to anti-GM1 and anti-GD1a antibodies and to motor and axonal forms, which is this node's mimicry route.

evidence.snippet: High titers of antibodies recognizing C. jejuni, consistent with recent infection, were found in the 2 patients tested.
evidence.explanation: Autopsy-confirmed cases of this subtype carried serology for recent C. jejuni infection, though only two selected fatal cases were tested.

edges/17.description: Antecedent enteritis supplies the sialylated lipooligosaccharide this node is built around, with the anti-GM1 and anti-GD1a response as the named intervening step. Both evidence items keep the partial grade this entry already assigned them, because neither isolates an effect size for this axonal subtype as opposed to the syndrome at large.

evidence.snippet: TF recommends intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) 0.4 g/kg for 5 days
evidence.explanation: The guideline establishes the regimen for non-ambulatory GBS. No randomized AMSAN-specific efficacy evidence was identified.

treatments/0.description: IVIG is one of two established immune treatments for GBS. The guideline regimen is 0.4 g/kg daily for five days, generally started within two weeks of weakness onset in a patient unable to walk unaided; selected patients may be treated at two to four weeks. Evidence and recommendations are GBS-wide, not AMSAN-specific.

evidence.snippet: a course of plasma exchange (PE) 12-15 L in four to five exchanges over 1-2 weeks
evidence.explanation: The guideline establishes the standard GBS regimen; no randomized AMSAN-specific treatment comparison was identified.

treatments/1.description: Plasma exchange is an established alternative first-line immune treatment for GBS. The guideline regimen is 12-15 L in four to five exchanges over one to two weeks, generally within four weeks of weakness onset when the patient cannot walk unaided. It is not routine rescue immediately after IVIG.

evidence.snippet: Respiratory function should be monitored in all patients
evidence.explanation: Consensus guidance supports proactive respiratory monitoring across GBS, including AMSAN.

evidence.snippet: patients should be monitored for swallowing and coughing difficulties.
evidence.explanation: Bulbar monitoring is part of GBS supportive care and is relevant to severe AMSAN.

treatments/2.description: All hospitalized patients require repeated respiratory assessment because dyspnea can be absent despite declining vital capacity. Monitoring also includes cough and swallow safety, heart rate, blood pressure, rhythm, bowel and bladder function, strength, and GBS disability. Rapid deterioration, bulbar weakness, dysautonomia, or adverse mEGRIS should lower the threshold for intensive-care transfer.

evidence.snippet: 10-30% require mechanical ventilation during the acute phase of the disease.
evidence.explanation: The GBS-wide guideline supports ventilation as a common severe-disease requirement without assigning this rate to AMSAN.

treatments/3.description: Invasive ventilation is supportive therapy for respiratory failure. It does not modify the immune attack, so respiratory monitoring and timely airway planning remain essential.

evidence.snippet: Start rehabilitation programme early
evidence.explanation: Consensus guidance supports multidisciplinary rehabilitation; controlled AMSAN-specific rehabilitation evidence is not available.

treatments/4.description: Rehabilitation should begin during hospitalization and continue after discharge as needed. Physical and occupational therapy, graded mobility and strengthening, positioning and contracture prevention, speech/swallow care, respiratory therapy, assistive devices, and psychosocial support are tailored to weakness, sensory loss, fatigue, pain, and bulbar or respiratory deficits.

evidence.snippet: weakly recommends gabapentinoids, tricyclic antidepressants or carbamazepine for treatment of pain
evidence.explanation: This is a weak GBS-wide recommendation and not an AMSAN-specific trial result.

treatments/5.description: Neuropathic, radicular, and nociceptive pain should be assessed repeatedly and treated while accounting for respiratory and autonomic vulnerability. The guideline weakly supports gabapentinoids, tricyclic antidepressants, or carbamazepine; drug choice and dose require individualized safety review.

evidence.snippet: acute motor axonal neuropathy, acute motor and sensory neuropathy and acute sensory neuropathy and possibly also a chronic disorder as multifocal motor neuropathy represent a spectrum of the same immunopathologic process.
evidence.explanation: This synthesis supports a shared nodal-to-axonal spectrum rather than fully independent mechanisms for AMAN and AMSAN.

evidence.snippet: represent the most severe end of a spectrum of immune attack directed toward epitopes on the axon.
evidence.explanation: Direct AMSAN pathology supports the severe-end-of-spectrum interpretation.

hypotheses/0.description: In the seropositive and especially C. jejuni-associated axonal GBS subset, molecular mimicry generates cross-reactive anti-ganglioside IgG. Antibody binding at nodal and axolemmal sites activates classical complement, producing a continuum from reversible nodal conduction failure to macrophage-associated irreversible motor and sensory axonal degeneration.

evidence.snippet: the electrodiagnostic subtype changed on serial NCS in 37.8% (Hadden) and 44.7% (Rajabally).
evidence.explanation: Frequent reclassification directly motivates the stability question.

evidence.snippet: represent the most severe end of a spectrum of immune attack directed toward epitopes on the axon.
evidence.explanation: Human pathology explicitly advances the spectrum interpretation.

open_questions/0.rationale: Fatal pathology supports genuine motor and sensory axonal destruction, but serial NCS shows frequent bidirectional subtype changes and no added value from electrodiagnostic subtyping. Resolving which patients have reversible nodal failure versus fixed sensory and motor axon loss matters more than a single early label.

evidence.snippet: Whether ganglioside-seronegative patients have other antibodies relevant to GBS is currently unclear.
evidence.explanation: The primer directly identifies the unresolved antigen problem.

open_questions/1.rationale: Ganglioside antibodies occur in only a subset of GBS, and routine testing has limited clinical value. Treating the canonical GM1/GD1a mechanism as universal would erase seronegative disease and mechanisms following non-C. jejuni antecedents.

evidence.snippet: new in vivo transgenic mouse model of AMAN
evidence.explanation: The model is explicitly AMAN rather than AMSAN.

evidence.snippet: wallerian-like degeneration of fibers in the ventral and dorsal roots
evidence.explanation: Human AMSAN pathology requires a model capable of both motor and sensory injury.

open_questions/2.rationale: Existing rabbit, transgenic-mouse, and ex vivo systems convincingly model motor-axon antibody/complement injury. Direct human AMSAN pathology instead shows dorsal as well as ventral root injury. A sensory-inclusive model is needed before subtype-specific mechanism or therapeutic claims are made.

evidence.snippet: recommends against using oral corticosteroids, and weakly recommends against using IV corticosteroids
evidence.explanation: The guideline directly recommends against corticosteroid therapy.

evidence.snippet: a second intravenous immunoglobulin course should not be considered for treatment of Guillain-Barre syndrome because of a poor prognosis.
evidence.explanation: The randomized SID-GBS trial found no benefit and more serious adverse events.

evidence.snippet: The combination of PE with IVIg did not confer a significant advantage.
evidence.explanation: The randomized comparison found no significant advantage for the immediate combination.

open_questions/3.rationale: These regimens can be mistaken for positive treatment options if represented as ordinary treatment nodes. Current guideline and randomized evidence do not support routine use for poor prognosis or initial non-response.

evidence.snippet: We report a kindred with adult-onset slowly progressive ataxia and polyneuropathy and with the heteroplasmic 8993T-->C mutation.
evidence.explanation: This is the defining report for OMIM 500010 and directly ties the heteroplasmic m.8993T>C MT-ATP6 variant to the adult-onset ataxia-plus-polyneuropathy phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Two point mutations (T>G and T>C) at the same 8993 nucleotide of mitochondrial DNA (at comparable mutant load), affecting the ATPase 6 subunit of the F1F0-ATPase, result in neurological phenotypes of variable severity in humans.
evidence.explanation: Locates the lesion in the ATPase 6 subunit of F1F0-ATP synthase and records that the two nucleotide-8993 substitutions differ in severity.

steps/1.description: The defining mitochondrial m.8993T>C missense variant substitutes proline for leucine at ATP6 residue 156. ATP6 encodes subunit a of ATP synthase. Related adult-ataxia variants m.9035T>C and m.9185T>C have distinct assay and clinical evidence; their results are qualified wherever used.

evidence.snippet: In our families, six patients had their genetic testing performed on leucocyte DNA, with heteroplasmy levels ranging from 90-99%.
evidence.explanation: Related m.9185T>C and m.9035T>C families include high-load adult presentations; blood load is not a universal predictor of onset.

evidence.snippet: There were marked phenotypic differences between family members, even between individuals with the greatest degrees of ectodermal and mesodermal heteroplasmy.
evidence.explanation: In an m.8993T>C family, measured heteroplasmy did not account for the within-family phenotypic spread, supporting the modulator role and the limits of load as a predictor. Graded INDIRECT because the cohort was diagnosed as NARP syndrome (MONDO:0010794), an entity this entry keeps distinct; the observation carries across because the modulator claim is about m.8993T>C heteroplasmy behaviour rather than about either phenotype.

evidence.snippet: they show very little tissue-dependent or age-dependent variation in
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews mtDNA-associated Leigh syndrome spectrum chapter: This statement specifically concerns m.8993T>G/C; it limits generic claims that blood load is unreliable for these variants.

steps/2.description: Mutant load modifies clinical expression but is not a universal onset clock or a fixed threshold. The defining adult proband had 89% mutant mtDNA in blood; related adult-ataxia pedigrees had 90–99% in leukocytes. GeneReviews describes relatively little tissue- or age-dependent heteroplasmy variation for m.8993T>C/G, unlike some other mtDNA variants. Differences among tissues can nevertheless occur, and high load does not reliably predict an individual phenotype. Nuclear, haplogroup and copy-number modifiers remain candidate explanations rather than demonstrated determinants here.

evidence.snippet: Both 8993T>G and 8993T>C mutations led to energy deprivation and ROS overproduction.
evidence.explanation: Measurements in patient lymphocytes, not neurons; the abstract reports both ATP-related energy deprivation and increased ROS.

evidence.snippet: We confirmed that the 4452T>C transition in tRNA(Met) represented a polymorphism; however, 9035T>C conversion in the ATP6 gene was responsible for a defective F(0)-ATPase.
evidence.explanation: Cybrid evidence that an ataxia-associated MT-ATP6 missense variant produces a defective F0-ATPase. Graded INDIRECT because this cybrid work used m.9035T>C, a different MT-ATP6 variant in the same adult-onset ataxia spectrum, not the m.8993T>C variant that defines this entry.

evidence.snippet: In mitochondria isolated from skin fibroblasts of both patients no decrease in oligomycin sensitive ATPase activity could be discerned either (see Table 1).
evidence.explanation: Negative result in primary m.9035T>C fibroblasts limits generalization of the earlier cybrid ATPase defect.

steps/3.description: The m.8993T>C ATP6 substitution perturbs ATP-synthase-related bioenergetics. In related m.9035T>C cybrids, F0-ATPase dysfunction was measured. Complex V subcomplexes in m.9035T>C patient material suggest altered assembly or stability, but that interpretation is provisional: oligomycin-sensitive ATP hydrolysis was normal in the later primary-fibroblast and muscle study. The assays and cellular backgrounds differ.

evidence.snippet: Both 8993T>G and 8993T>C mutations led to energy deprivation and ROS overproduction.
evidence.explanation: Measurements in patient lymphocytes, not neurons; the abstract reports both ATP-related energy deprivation and increased ROS.

evidence.snippet: They had less than half of the steady-state content of ATP and nearly an 8-fold higher basal level of reactive oxygen species (ROS).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the combined ATP shortfall and ROS burden in cybrids carrying an MT-ATP6 ataxia variant. Graded INDIRECT because the cybrids carried m.9035T>C.

steps/4.description: Energy deprivation was measured in m.8993T>C patient lymphocytes. Related m.9035T>C cybrids had less than half the control steady-state ATP content. These are non-neuronal experimental results; neuronal ATP depletion in the adult syndrome has not been directly measured.

evidence.snippet: The 8993T>G change mainly induces an energy deficiency, whereas the 8993T>C favours an increased ROS production.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the ROS-weighted balance of the bioenergetic lesion for the m.8993T>C variant that defines this entry.

evidence.snippet: They had less than half of the steady-state content of ATP and nearly an 8-fold higher basal level of reactive oxygen species (ROS).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the combined ATP shortfall and ROS burden in cybrids carrying an MT-ATP6 ataxia variant. Graded INDIRECT because the cybrids carried m.9035T>C.

steps/5.description: Patient lymphocytes carrying m.8993T>C showed increased ROS production, with a different balance between ROS and energy deprivation than m.8993T>G. Related m.9035T>C cybrids showed markedly increased ROS and stress-induced cell death. These experiments do not establish that ROS determines adult onset or prove neuronal injury in vivo.

evidence.snippet: Three siblings were clinically examined. Two of them presented with an adult or late-onset slowly pro- gressive gait ataxia and dysarthria, and all three had peripheral axonal neuropathy. Ataxia was considered both cerebellar and sensory in origin.
evidence.explanation: Rantamäki et al. 2005 original article reprinted in the author thesis, pp. 337–340: Two of three examined adults had overt ataxia/dysarthria, while all three had peripheral axonal neuropathy; this selected family is not a population-frequency estimate.

evidence.snippet: EMG-NCS revealed varying degrees of length-dependent sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy.
evidence.explanation: Electrophysiological demonstration of length-dependent axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy in an m.8993T>C family. Graded INDIRECT because that family was diagnosed as NARP syndrome (MONDO:0010794), which this entry curates as a separate entity and a differential.

steps/6.description: Axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy was demonstrated electrophysiologically in all three examined adults in the defining kindred, with sensory loss, absent ankle reflexes and weakness.
