Recorded as PARTIAL because the study measures telomere and DNA-damage biology in those cells rather than testing the activation step itself.

steps/7.description: Where the fibrosing members of the family converge on the conserved fibrotic response. Injured alveolar epithelium fails to re-epithelialise and instead releases profibrotic signals that drive fibroblasts into collagen-secreting myofibroblasts. This node is deliberately generic: the disease-specific upstream biology that feeds it in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis — telomere attrition, AT2 senescence, aberrant basaloid cells, MUC5B — is curated on the IPF entry and is not re-derived here.

evidence.snippet: PPF was defined as at least two of three criteria (worsening symptoms, radiological progression, and physiological progression) occurring within the past year with no alternative explanation in a patient with an ILD other than IPF.
evidence.explanation: The operational definition of the shared progressive behaviour this node models, and the explicit statement that it is recognised in interstitial lung diseases other than IPF.

evidence.snippet: Antifibrotic agents should be considered in a condition, termed progressive pulmonary fibrosis, where pulmonary fibrosis progressively worsens.
evidence.explanation: Shows the behaviour-based rule being applied to a non-IPF member of the family, which is the practical consequence of modelling this outcome at the root rather than per entity.

evidence.snippet: The definition of PF-ILD includes symptom progression, PFT decline, and extension of chest high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) findings.
evidence.explanation: Independently states the three-domain composite that operationalises progression, corroborating the guideline definition.

steps/8.description: The shared adverse outcome of the family and the reason its members are managed together despite their different lesions. Accumulating matrix destroys alveolar architecture, and a subset of every fibrosing entity — including entities with an otherwise favourable prognosis — declines on symptoms, physiology, and imaging in the way IPF does. The 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT guideline made this a defined, treatable behaviour rather than a descriptive impression, and it is behaviour, not the original histopathologic label, that then governs antifibrotic therapy.

edges/5.description: The chronic fibrosing arm of the classification (UIP in IPF, and the fibrotic NSIP pattern) enters the fibrotic response directly rather than through an intervening acute or inflammatory lesion.

edges/6.description: The organizing phase that follows acute diffuse alveolar damage feeds the same fibroblast-driven remodelling as the chronic fibrosing entities.

evidence.snippet: Respiratory bronchiolitis-associated ILD mainly affects smokers, showing ground-glass opacities on chest computed tomography (CT) scans and pigmented macrophages in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid.
evidence.explanation: Links the exposure directly to the macrophage lesion this edge targets.

edges/8.description: Tobacco smoke is the proximate cause of the pigmented-macrophage lesion that defines the smoking-related arm of the classification.

evidence.snippet: A defining feature of COP is steroid-responsiveness, and most experts recommend prolonged corticosteroid courses (6-12 months).
evidence.explanation: Establishes steroid responsiveness as definitional for the organizing entity and gives the treatment duration.

evidence.snippet: Lymphoid interstitial pneumonia involves lymphocytic proliferation and is associated with autoimmune diseases or infections, treated with corticosteroids.
evidence.explanation: Extends the same therapy to the lymphoid entity, the other cellular member of the family.

treatments/0.description: First-line for the inflammatory and organizing entities — COP above all, and LIP — where the lesion is cellular and the alveolar scaffold is intact. Deliberately not a family-wide recommendation: the same therapy does not benefit the chronic fibrosing entities, which is one practical reason the IIP root cannot be treated as a single disease.

evidence.snippet: The hallmark pathological features are presence of polypoid granulation tissue, or Masson bodies, in the alveolar spaces, with lung architecture preserved in most patients with good clinical outcomes poststeroid treatment.
evidence.explanation: Ties the good post-steroid outcome directly to the intra-alveolar granulation-tissue lesion this treatment targets.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Corticosteroids suppress the fibroblastic organizing lesion while the alveolar architecture is still intact, allowing it to resolve.

evidence.snippet: Smoking cessation is essential for treatment, with corticosteroids used for severe cases.
evidence.explanation: States smoking cessation as the essential treatment for the smoking-related arm, with steroids reserved for severe disease.

treatments/1.description: First-line and potentially disease-modifying for RB-ILD and DIP. The only intervention in the family that removes a driver rather than modulating a response, and the reason the smoking-related entities are separated out. NCIT has no clinical-intervention term for smoking cessation — NCIT:C17427 is classified under Behavior, not under Clinical Intervention or Procedure — so the action is left as free text rather than bound to an unreachable term.

evidence.snippet: Respiratory bronchiolitis-associated ILD mainly affects smokers, showing ground-glass opacities on chest computed tomography (CT) scans and pigmented macrophages in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the smoking-to-macrophage-lesion link that makes removing the exposure a mechanism-directed intervention on this node.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Removing the exposure removes the stimulus for the pigmented-macrophage accumulation that constitutes the lesion.

evidence.snippet: A conditional recommendation was made for nintedanib, and additional research into pirfenidone was recommended.
evidence.explanation: The guideline recommendation that attaches antifibrotic therapy to the progressive-fibrosis behaviour rather than to a single entity.

treatments/2.description: Antifibrotic tyrosine kinase inhibitor. Recommended for interstitial lung disease other than IPF that meets the progressive-pulmonary-fibrosis criteria, so the indication is keyed to observed disease behaviour rather than to the original histopathologic label.

evidence.snippet: A conditional recommendation was made for nintedanib, and additional research into pirfenidone was recommended.
evidence.explanation: The recommendation is made for the progressive-pulmonary-fibrosis behaviour that this target node models.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Nintedanib slows the fibrotic progression that defines the PPF behaviour, without reversing established fibrosis.

evidence.snippet: Acute interstitial pneumonia resembles acute respiratory distress syndrome but occurs without a clear cause and is managed with supportive care.
evidence.explanation: States supportive care as the management of the acute entity, in the absence of a disease-modifying option.

treatments/3.description: The mainstay for acute interstitial pneumonia, where no therapy has been shown to alter the course, and a component of care across the family (supplemental oxygen when hypoxemic, symptom-directed and palliative measures). Pulmonary rehabilitation, previously named only inside this description, is now curated as its own treatment.

evidence.snippet: Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is a beneficial intervention for people with interstitial lung disease (ILD); however, the effect of PR on survival is unclear.
evidence.explanation: States both the established benefit and the explicit limit of the evidence, which is why this entry claims function and quality of life but not survival.

evidence.snippet: Participation in PR among people with ILD may impact survival at 5 years.
evidence.explanation: The hedged survival signal from a pooled analysis of two randomized trials. Recorded as PARTIAL because the unadjusted comparison was not significant and no difference remained at ten years.

treatments/4.description: Structured supervised exercise training and education. Applies across the family rather than to one entity, and is also the standard preparation for transplant candidates. The functional and quality-of-life benefit is established; a survival benefit is suggested at five years but is not settled, and the entry does not claim one.

evidence.snippet: Despite this increase many patients with ILD who would potentially benefit from lung transplant are either not referred or referred too late.
evidence.explanation: Documents late referral as the practical limiting factor, supporting the description's emphasis on referral timing as a management decision.

evidence.snippet: Unfortunately, the number of potential lung transplant recipients exceeds available donor organs and some patients will die without transplant.
evidence.explanation: Documents the donor-supply constraint that bounds this therapy's reach.

treatments/5.description: The only intervention that replaces the fibrotic lung rather than slowing its remodelling, and the definitive therapy for advanced fibrotic disease across this family rather than for one entity. Curated here rather than delegated to the IPF entry for exactly that reason. Access is limited by donor supply and by late referral, so timing of referral is itself a management decision.

evidence.snippet: Interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) are now the most common indication for lung transplant internationally.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that transplantation is directed at this disease family as a whole, which is what justifies attaching it to the shared progressive-fibrosis node rather than to a single entity.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: Transplantation does not act on the fibrotic mechanism at all; it removes the diseased organ, so the causal chain modelled here is bypassed rather than inhibited. BYPASSES is used deliberately in preference to INHIBITS, which would misstate the mechanism.

evidence.snippet: A substantial percentage of patients with IIP are difficult to classify, often due to mixed patterns of lung injury.
evidence.explanation: The classification's own authors record the limitation this gap is about.

open_questions/0.rationale: The entire classification rests on the premise that the injured lung adopts one of a small number of discrete patterns. The 2013 ATS/ERS update records that a substantial percentage of patients defeat that premise, usually because more than one pattern is present in the same lung. This matters for a knowledge base: if the mixed cases are a continuum rather than a set of undiscovered entities, then the pattern nodes modelled here are convenient landmarks on a spectrum rather than mutually exclusive states, and a curated entry should not imply that a patient occupies exactly one of them.

evidence.snippet: A classification based on observed disease behavior is proposed for patients who are difficult to classify or for entities with heterogeneity in clinical course.
evidence.explanation: The behaviour-based alternative is proposed in the classification statement itself, which is what makes this a live tension rather than a settled question.

evidence.snippet: The clinical course of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and nonspecific interstitial pneumonia is recognized to be heterogeneous.
evidence.explanation: Names the heterogeneity within single entities that makes the pattern label an incomplete predictor of course.

open_questions/1.rationale: The 2013 update proposed a behaviour-based classification precisely for the patients and entities the pattern-based scheme handles badly, and the 2022 guideline then defined progressive pulmonary fibrosis as a behaviour that cuts across entities and carries its own treatment recommendation. The result is a family whose members are named on one axis and treated on another. Which axis a mechanism knowledge base should treat as primary is unresolved, and the answer determines whether progressive pulmonary fibrosis is modelled as a shared outcome node (as here) or as a separate cross-cutting entity.

evidence.snippet: The risk of IPF was significantly higher in current and former smokers than in never smokers, with an aHR of 1.66 (95% CI 1.61 to 1.72) and 1.42 (95% CI 1.37 to 1.48), respectively.
evidence.explanation: Korean nationwide claims cohort supports temporality and an exposure association; diagnosis was based on codes and claims.

evidence.snippet: Ever smoking tobacco was associated with increased risk of IPF: OR 2.20 (95% CI 1.74 to 2.79)
evidence.explanation: Independent Australian case-control study included 503 cases and 902 population controls.

evidence.snippet: After adjustment for environmental and military exposures and smoking history, the OR for metal dust exposure was 4.97 (95%CI 1.36-18.17) in multiple logistic regression analysis.
evidence.explanation: Korean matched case-control study included 78 cases and 78 controls; the interval is wide.

evidence.snippet: However occupational exposures to other specific organic, mineral or metal dusts were not associated with IPF.
evidence.explanation: The larger Australian study did not replicate associations with these specific dust categories.

evidence.snippet: respirable dust (OR 1.38; 1.04 to 1.82) and asbestos (OR 1.57; 1.15 to 2.15) were independently associated with increased risk of IPF.
evidence.explanation: Respirable-dust association was observed even though specific metal-dust categories were null.

evidence.snippet: ORs and PAFs, respectively, were found to be 1.6 and 7% for metal dust, 1.6 and 3% for wood dust, 1.8 and 14% for agricultural dust, and 1.8 and 4% for silica dust.
evidence.explanation: Meta-analysis reports pooled associations; attributable fractions rely on causal assumptions and are not demonstrated prevention effects.

evidence.snippet: Smoking adjustments: general dust (1.45 (1.04-2.03)/organic dust (2.5 (1.49-4.22)/metals (1.87 (1.16-3)/wood dust OR: 1.16 (0.86-1.61)/pesticide exposure 2.4 (0.84-6.9) were calculated.
evidence.explanation: Smoking-adjusted analysis in an earlier meta-analysis was compatible with no wood-dust association, limiting certainty.

evidence.snippet: asbestos (OR 1.57; 1.15 to 2.15) were independently associated with increased risk of IPF.
evidence.explanation: Reported association concerns patients classified as IPF; it does not erase the separate diagnosis of asbestosis.

evidence.snippet: Exclusion of other known causes of ILD (e.g., domestic and occupational environmental exposures, connective tissue disease, and drug toxicity).
evidence.explanation: Clinically established exposure-caused ILD must be excluded before assigning IPF.

evidence.snippet: ORs and PAFs, respectively, were found to be 1.6 and 7% for metal dust, 1.6 and 3% for wood dust, 1.8 and 14% for agricultural dust, and 1.8 and 4% for silica dust.
evidence.explanation: Pooled occupational associations include agricultural dust, with heterogeneity in exposure assessment and disease definition.

evidence.snippet: The major differential diagnostic considerations include UIP in other clinical settings such as connective tissue diseases, chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (extrinsic allergic alveolitis), and pneumoconioses (especially asbestosis).
evidence.explanation: Antigen-mediated hypersensitivity pneumonitis is a distinct cause of fibrosis, even with a UIP pattern.

evidence.snippet: Genetic and pharmacological inhibition in AT2 cells of carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1a (CPT1a), the rate-limiting enzyme of FAO, promoted mitochondrial dysfunction and acquisition of aberrant intermediate states expressing basaloid, and airway secretory cell markers SCGB1A1 and SCGB3A2.
evidence.explanation: CPT1a perturbation changes epithelial metabolism and cell states in experimental models.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, mice with deficiency of CPT1a in AT2 cells show enhanced susceptibility to developing lung fibrosis with an accumulation of epithelial cells expressing markers of intermediate cells, airway secretory cells, and senescence.
evidence.explanation: AT2-specific metabolic deficiency amplifies injury-associated fibrosis; it is not an established monogenic cause of human IPF.

steps/13.description: FAO gene expression is reduced in human IPF alveolar epithelium. Experimental CPT1a deficiency produces mitochondrial dysfunction, lower SMAD7 and increased TGF-beta signaling, abnormal epithelial intermediates and increased injury susceptibility. These findings support a metabolic contribution to abnormal repair without proving that FAO loss is the initiating event in human IPF.

evidence.snippet: interleukin-11 (IL11) is up-regulated in the lung of patients with IPF, associated with disease severity, and IL-11 is secreted from IPF fibroblasts
evidence.explanation: Establishes IL-11 up-regulation in patient IPF lung and its secretion by IPF fibroblasts, grounding this node in human disease. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL (patient lung tissue).

evidence.snippet: IL-11 stimulates lung fibroblasts to become invasive actin alpha 2, smooth muscle-positive (ACTA2+), collagen-secreting myofibroblasts in an extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK)-dependent, posttranscriptional manner
evidence.explanation: Directly evidences the IL-11 to ERK receptor-signalling arm driving fibroblast-to-myofibroblast conversion modeled by this node. Evidence source is IN_VITRO (cultured lung fibroblasts).

evidence.snippet: anti-IL-11 treatment diminished lung inflammation and reversed lung fibrosis while inhibiting ERK and SMAD activation in mice
evidence.explanation: Shows pharmacological IL-11 inhibition reverses lung fibrosis and lowers ERK activation in vivo, validating the drug-target link on this node. Evidence source is MODEL_ORGANISM (bleomycin mouse model).

steps/14.description: IL-11 is increased in human IPF lungs and secreted by IPF fibroblasts. In cultured lung fibroblasts it promotes ERK-dependent, posttranscriptional myofibroblast conversion. Neutralizing IL-11 reverses fibrosis in a mouse model; efficacy in human IPF is not established by that experiment.

evidence.snippet: Six probands (8%) had heterozygous mutations in hTERT or hTR; mutant telomerase resulted in short telomeres.
evidence.explanation: The familial cohort demonstrates pathogenic telomerase variants and short telomeres. Unaffected carriers also had short telomeres, showing incomplete disease penetrance.

evidence.snippet: These results demonstrate that prolonged telomere dysfunction in type II AECs, but not collagen-expressing cells, leads to age-dependent lung remodeling and fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: Conditional TRF1 deletion causes spontaneous fibrosis after prolonged epithelial telomere dysfunction; this severe uncapping model is distinct from ordinary age-related shortening.

evidence.snippet: PARN and RTEL1 mutation carriers had shortened leukocyte telomere lengths, and we observed epigenetic inheritance of short telomeres in family members.
evidence.explanation: Human pedigrees link rare variants to telomere dysfunction and familial pulmonary fibrosis.

evidence.snippet: Reduced telomere length may be identified in a quarter of patients with sporadic idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and half of those cases with family aggregation
evidence.explanation: A clinical review quantifying how often measurably short telomeres are detected, with the expected enrichment in familial disease. This supports treating this node as a susceptibility route present in a subset rather than in all patients. The figure describes detectable shortening in the assayed compartment, usually leukocytes, and is not a measurement of the fraction of IPF mediated by alveolar epithelial senescence.

steps/15.description: Pathogenic telomere-maintenance variants and age-related shortening can produce dysfunctional telomeres and persistent DNA-damage signaling in alveolar epithelial cells. The human genetic evidence supports susceptibility, with incomplete penetrance. Experimental shelterin/TRF1 uncapping can induce spontaneous lung fibrosis, whereas AT2-specific TERT loss increases bleomycin susceptibility without measurable telomere shortening in one model. These perturbations must not be treated as interchangeable demonstrations of physiological telomere attrition.

evidence.snippet: We show that expression of two SP-A1 (R219W and R242*) and three SP-C (I73T, M71V, and L188Q) variant proteins lead to the secretion of the profibrotic latent transforming growth factor (TGF)-β1 in lung epithelial cell lines.
evidence.explanation: Surfactant variants can promote TGF-beta secretion through variant-dependent pathways.

evidence.snippet: Expression of L188Q SFTPC induced ER stress, as determined by increased expression of heavy-chain Ig binding protein (BiP) and splicing of X-box binding protein 1 (XBP1) mRNA, but no lung fibrosis was identified in the absence of a second profibrotic stimulus.
evidence.explanation: The second-hit requirement is specific to this mutant-surfactant model.

evidence.snippet: ER stress and UPR activation are found in the alveolar epithelium in patients with IPF and could contribute to disease progression.
evidence.explanation: Human tissue supports pathway presence; the conditional language is retained.

evidence.snippet: The mutation (p.Trp211Arg), which segregates with a disease phenotype characterized by either isolated IIP/IPF, or IPF associated with lung adenocarcinoma
evidence.explanation: A multigenerational family and secretion experiments support a rare SFTPA1-related subset; this is distinct from the common SP-A1 variant tested in the TGF-beta secretion study.

steps/16.description: Rare surfactant variants predispose a subset of familial interstitial lung disease, sometimes classified as IPF. Misprocessing and endoplasmic-reticulum stress can compromise AT2 function, but variants differ: SP-A1 R219W-driven TGF-beta secretion is UPR dependent, whereas SP-C I73T and M71V secretion is largely UPR independent. L188Q SFTPC-induced ER stress increases bleomycin susceptibility without spontaneous fibrosis in one mouse model. Herpesvirus colocalization with UPR markers in human tissue does not establish viral causation.

evidence.snippet: it has been suggested that repeated microinjuries of epithelial cells induce a wound healing response, during which fibroblasts differentiate into myofibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: This review directly supports repetitive epithelial injury as the initiating trigger for maladaptive wound healing in IPF.

evidence.snippet: Apoptosis, senescence, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, endothelial-mesenchymal transition, and epithelial cell migration have been shown to play a key role in IPF-associated tissue remodeling.
evidence.explanation: This review links epithelial apoptosis and senescence to the abnormal remodeling response after lung injury in IPF.

steps/17.description: Recurrent injury to alveolar epithelial cells, particularly type II pneumocytes, initiates a dysregulated wound-healing response that fails to restore normal alveolar architecture and instead drives fibrotic remodeling.

evidence.snippet: In contrast, mice with lung epithelial cell-specific deletion of CCL12 were protected from bleomycin-induced fibrosis and had expression of CCL2 and CCL7 similar to that of control mice treated with bleomycin. Deletion of CCL12 within AECs led to decreased recruitment of exudate macrophages.
evidence.explanation: Epithelial CCL12 contributes to macrophage recruitment in this mouse injury model; global CCL12 deletion was not protective and this is not universal immune necessity.

evidence.snippet: Together, these findings reveal a novel role of SIRT3 in pro-resolution macrophage functions that restore susceptibility to apoptosis in fibroblasts via a FoxO3a-dependent mechanism.
evidence.explanation: Macrophage-dependent effects can also favor resolution in the SIRT3 restoration model.

steps/18.description: Recruited monocyte-derived macrophages can amplify fibrosis after epithelial injury through CCR2-dependent pathways. Macrophage behavior changes with cell state and disease phase: some macrophage-derived signals promote resolution and fibroblast apoptosis. Neither a uniformly profibrotic macrophage role nor universal immune dependence follows from these models.

evidence.snippet: Chronic canonical WNT/β-catenin activation for up to 7 days in primary ATII cells as well as alveolar epithelial cell lines induced a robust cellular senescence, whereas the non-canonical ligand WNT5A was not able to induce cellular senescence.
evidence.explanation: Sustained canonical signaling induces senescence in these cultures; telomere independence was not directly tested.

evidence.snippet: In 18 of 20 cases of IPF/UIP investigated on serial sections, nuclear beta-catenin immunoreactivity and abnormal levels of cyclin-D1 and matrilysin were demonstrated in proliferative bronchiolar lesions (basal-cell hyperplasia, squamous metaplasia, bronchiolization, honeycombing)
evidence.explanation: Immunohistochemistry places the pathway readout, nuclear beta-catenin with induction of the targets cyclin-D1 and matrilysin, in human IPF/UIP tissue, and the same study reports these features absent from normal lung and from other fibrosing pneumonias. It localizes activation to proliferative bronchiolar and honeycomb lesions rather than to alveolar type II cells specifically, so it grounds the node in the human disease without establishing the AT2 route tested in culture.

steps/19.description: Persistent canonical WNT/beta-catenin activation can shift AT2 cells toward senescence and impaired progenitor behavior in cultures and precision-cut lung slices. Acute and chronic stimulation differ. WNT5A did not reproduce the canonical senescence response in the cited assay; this does not exclude other profibrotic WNT5A actions.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, ectopic mtDNA augmented cGAS-dependent senescence of Ctrl-AECs, whereas DNAse I treatment diminished IPF-AEC senescence.
evidence.explanation: Self-DNA perturbations and cGAS inhibition support senescence amplification in cultured epithelial cells.

steps/20.description: Mitochondrial DNA accumulation in cytosol and extracellular medium accompanies stressed IPF epithelial cultures. cGAS inhibition, RNA interference and DNase experiments support self-DNA-dependent senescence amplification. The study does not demonstrate obligatory STING activation or a requirement for recruited immune cells in every fibrosis model.

evidence.snippet: Accumulating evidence supports bidirectional gut-lung axis interactions potentially mediated by the microbiota. Alterations in the gut microbiome have been associated with the onset and severity of interstitial lung disease.
evidence.explanation: Review-level evidence summarizes clinical associations and preclinical gut-lung mechanisms; it does not establish the specified causal sequence or direction in human IPF.

evidence.snippet: Preclinical studies demonstrate that gut dysbiosis is associated with altered immune responses, increased pro-inflammatory cytokines, and enhanced fibrotic pathways, with mechanistic evidence suggesting the involvement of specific microbial metabolites (short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and immune mediators.
evidence.explanation: Review-level evidence summarizes clinical associations and preclinical gut-lung mechanisms; it does not establish the specified causal sequence or direction in human IPF.

steps/21.description: Altered gut microbial composition and metabolites have been associated with interstitial lung disease, and preclinical models suggest effects on immune responses and fibrosis. Directionality, specific mediators and independence from diet, disease severity and antifibrotic treatment remain unresolved in human IPF. This is an emerging modifier rather than an established universal upstream mechanism.

evidence.snippet: A common polymorphism in the promoter of MUC5B is associated with familial interstitial pneumonia and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: This human case-control study identifies the MUC5B promoter variant rs35705950 as a major inherited susceptibility factor for IPF.

evidence.snippet: In mice, we demonstrate that Muc5b concentration in bronchoalveolar epithelia is related to impaired mucociliary clearance (MCC) and to the extent and persistence of bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: Muc5b overexpression is a susceptibility amplifier in an injury model, not proof that this allele alone initiates fibrosis in humans.

steps/22.description: The common MUC5B promoter risk allele increases pulmonary expression. Distal-airspace MUC5B overexpression impairs clearance and worsens persistent fibrosis after bleomycin in mice. This supplies a genetic susceptibility route distinct from telomere dysfunction; interaction with short leukocyte telomeres has been studied epidemiologically but its cellular mechanism remains unresolved.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that prevention of PDGFRα+ fibroblast apoptosis by conditional BCL-2 expression leads to the emergence and persistence of senescent, pro-fibrotic fibroblasts along with enduring, pathologic fibrotic lung remodeling.
evidence.explanation: Conditional anti-apoptotic signaling demonstrates a fibroblast persistence route in mice, not universal BCL-2 dependence in humans.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrated that nonsenescent lung myofibroblasts maintained the capacity for dedifferentiation, whereas senescent/IPF myofibroblasts exhibited an impaired capacity for dedifferentiation.
evidence.explanation: Cultured IPF fibroblasts show impaired fate reversal.

evidence.snippet: Nox4 mediated senescence and apoptosis resistance in IPF fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Experimental fibroblast perturbations support redox-dependent persistence.

steps/23.description: Aging-associated myofibroblasts can fail to dedifferentiate and become resistant to apoptosis. NOX4/NRF2 redox imbalance, sustained MyoD and BCL-2-dependent survival support persistence in experimental systems. Human IPF fibroblasts share aspects of these states. Senescence therefore contributes through mesenchymal persistence as well as epithelial dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: Loss of endothelial ERG ... impairs lung fibrosis resolution in young mice in vivo.
evidence.explanation: Conditional endothelial ERG loss impairs fibrosis resolution in mice; the separate in-vitro edge quotes the fibroblast-activation finding.

steps/24.description: Endothelial ERG dysregulation and capillary cell-state changes accompany aging and fibrotic repair. Conditional endothelial ERG loss impairs fibrosis resolution in mice and enhances paracrine fibroblast activation in culture. Human transcriptional overlap supports relevance but does not establish an independent initiating vascular lesion in all IPF.

evidence.snippet: bleomycin causes DNA damage and activates p53 signaling in AT2-lineage cells, leading to AT2-to-AT1 transition-like state with a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Among SASP-related factors, TGF-β plays an exclusive role in promoting lung fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation. Moreover, the autocrine TGF-β-positive feedback loop in AT2-lineage cells is a critical cellular system in non-inflammatory lung fibrogenesis.
evidence.explanation: The immune-cell-free organoid experiment establishes epithelial-fibroblast sufficiency under bleomycin stimulation; accompanying mouse genetics do not imply immune independence of whole-animal disease.

evidence.snippet: Recurrent alveolar epithelial cell (AEC) injury may occur in the context of predisposing factors (e.g., genetic, environmental, epigenetic, immunologic, and gerontologic), leading to metabolic dysfunction, senescence, aberrant epithelial cell activation, and dysregulated epithelial repair.
evidence.explanation: Annual Review of Pathology 2022 review places AT2 senescence as a consequence of recurrent injury that bridges injury to downstream fibrotic mechanisms.

evidence.snippet: We used conditional loss of Sin3a in adult mouse AT2 cells to initiate a program of p53-dependent cellular senescence, AT2 cell depletion, and spontaneous, progressive pulmonary fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: An AT2-directed genetic perturbation produces spontaneous progressive fibrosis without bleomycin; it does not establish immune independence or the initiating lesion in all human IPF.

steps/25.description: AT2-lineage cells can enter a stress-associated senescent state with reduced regenerative capacity and a secretory program that activates fibroblasts. DNA damage, telomere dysfunction, chronic Wnt signaling and metabolic stress are candidate upstream routes. Bleomycin-treated epithelial-fibroblast organoids show autocrine TGF-beta feedback and paracrine myofibroblast induction without immune cells. In vivo models establish senescence as a possible proximal driver, while the contribution of immune recruitment varies by model and cannot be declared universally necessary or dispensable.

evidence.snippet: Short telomeres limit tissue renewal capacity in the lung and germ-line mutations in telomerase components, hTERT and hTR, underlie inheritance in a subset of families with IPF.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that short telomeres limit lung tissue-renewal capacity, supporting exhaustion of the alveolar type II progenitor pool. Evidence source is HUMAN_CLINICAL (patient telomere-length study).

evidence.snippet: We establish that senescence rather than loss of AT2 cells promotes progressive fibrosis and show that either genetic or pharmacologic interventions targeting p53 activation or senescence block fibrogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Senescence-associated dysfunction cannot be reduced to simple progenitor depletion.

steps/26.description: AT2 cells normally regenerate the alveolar epithelium. Senescence and telomere dysfunction impair renewal and can deplete functional progenitors. Cell loss and a persistent senescent secretory state are distinct mechanisms: the Sin3a model distinguishes progressive senescence-associated fibrosis from transient remodeling after AT2 ablation.

evidence.snippet: Within both the IPF and SSc-ILD samples we identified a small population of the recently described aberrant basaloid cells (or KRT5-/KRT17+ cells), with no cells sharing this distinct transcriptome amongst the control samples
evidence.explanation: Human single-cell data identify this population in both IPF and SSc-ILD, so it is not specific to IPF and does not establish senescence-to-basaloid lineage causality.

evidence.snippet: These studies have uncovered a novel type of AEC with characteristics of an aberrant basal cell, which may disrupt normal epithelial repair and propagate a profibrotic phenotype.
evidence.explanation: Annual Review of Pathology 2022 review identifies the aberrant basaloid cell population as mechanistically relevant to IPF pathogenesis through disruption of normal epithelial repair.

evidence.snippet: Among epithelial cells enriched in IPF, we identify a previously unidentified population of aberrant basaloid cells that coexpress basal epithelial, mesenchymal, senescence, and developmental markers and are located at the edge of myofibroblast foci in the IPF lung.
evidence.explanation: Single-cell and histologic localization demonstrate a disease-associated state, not causal lineage conversion.

evidence.snippet: Using integrated single nucleus ATAC- and RNA-sequencing on human lungs and an in vitro model of dysplastic repair, we identify two distinct regenerative trajectories for alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells: a resolvable euplastic repair trajectory and a persistent, non-resolving dysplastic repair trajectory. The latter is governed by a spatially restricted ITGB6/TGFβ1/SMAD3 signaling axis in fibrotic regions of IPF lungs and in murine lungs characterized by chronic epithelial remodeling.
evidence.explanation: Integrated human data and experimental dysplastic-repair models identify TGF-beta/SMAD3 regulation; human observational evidence alone does not establish temporal initiation.

evidence.snippet: Here we demonstrate that human alveolar type 2 cells (hAEC2s), unlike murine AEC2s, transdifferentiate into basal cells in response to fibrotic signalling in the lung mesenchyme, in vitro and in vivo.
evidence.explanation: Source for this node's statement that human AT2 cultures can undergo a basal transition under defined signaling conditions. The demonstration rests on primary and iPSC-derived human AT2 organoid co-culture with adult human lung mesenchyme, confirmed after xenotransplantation into injured mouse lung. Two constraints are worth recording: the transition is driven by mesenchymal TGF-beta1 and BMP antagonism rather than by AT2 senescence, and murine AT2 cells under identical conditions did not transdifferentiate, so mouse lineage-tracing results do not transfer to human disease.

steps/27.description: KRT5-negative/KRT17-positive aberrant basaloid epithelial cells coexpress basal, mesenchymal and senescence-related markers and occur near myofibroblast foci in fibrotic human lungs. Their transcriptome is a disease-associated state rather than proof of epithelial conversion into fibroblasts. Human AT2 cultures can undergo a basal transition under defined signaling conditions, but the origin and causal contribution of every basaloid cell population in human IPF remain unresolved.

evidence.snippet: TGF-β is a critical cytokine that drives development of fibrosis.

steps/28.description: Resident mesenchymal cells become matrix-producing myofibroblasts in response to profibrotic mediators including TGF-beta and IL-11 and mechanical signals from matrix. evidence.snippet: These data are consistent with SFTPA2 germline mutations that interfere with protein trafficking and cause familial IPF and lung cancer.
evidence.explanation: Rare pathogenic variants cause familial fibrosis with lung adenocarcinoma susceptibility; this is a specific genetic subset, not a universal IPF mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Specifically, heterozygous germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants (PGVs) in SFTPA1 and SFTPA2, which encode surfactant proteins SP-A1 and SP-A2, can result in a range of outcomes from asymptomatic cases to severe lung fibrosis and adenocarcinoma, with high mortality risks
evidence.explanation: The pedigree study supports age-dependent variable disease expression. Pooled gene estimates, missing exposure data and competing-risk limitations prevent treating its penetrance numbers as universal IPF risks.

genes/6.notes: Rare pathogenic variants cause familial fibrosis with lung adenocarcinoma susceptibility; this is a specific genetic subset, not a universal IPF mechanism.

evidence.snippet: The mutation (p.Trp211Arg), which segregates with a disease phenotype characterized by either isolated IIP/IPF, or IPF associated with lung adenocarcinoma
evidence.explanation: A multigenerational family and secretion experiments support a rare SFTPA1-related subset; this is distinct from the common SP-A1 variant tested in the TGF-beta secretion study.

genes/7.notes: Rare pathogenic variants can cause familial interstitial pneumonia/IPF with lung adenocarcinoma susceptibility. Evidence comes from limited pedigrees and functional secretion studies; it is not interchangeable with SFTPA2 or with common SFTPA1 polymorphisms.

evidence.snippet: Pirfenidone, as compared with placebo, reduced disease progression, as reflected by lung function, exercise tolerance, and progression-free survival, in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: The ASCEND phase 3 trial shows pirfenidone slows clinical progression in IPF.

treatments/0.description: Oral antifibrotic therapy that slows clinical progression and FVC decline. It is not established to reverse existing scarring. Gastrointestinal and skin adverse effects and liver monitoring affect use.

evidence.snippet: Pirfenidone reduced fibroblast proliferation and attenuated TGF-β-induced α-smooth muscle actin (SMA) and pro-collagen (Col)-I mRNA and protein levels.
evidence.explanation: Primary human lung fibroblast experiments support an antifibrotic cellular effect; the direct molecular target and mediation of human benefit are not established.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Attenuates TGF-beta-stimulated fibroblast activation in culture; clinical slowing of progression is independently supported by ASCEND.

evidence.snippet: In patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, nintedanib reduced the decline in FVC, which is consistent with a slowing of disease progression
evidence.explanation: The INPULSIS phase 3 trials show nintedanib slows lung function decline in IPF.

treatments/1.description: Antifibrotic tyrosine kinase inhibitor that slows the rate of forced vital capacity decline in IPF.

evidence.snippet: Data from in vitro studies have shown that nintedanib interferes with processes active in fibrosis such as fibroblast proliferation, migration and differentiation, and the secretion of ECM.
evidence.explanation: The pharmacology review summarizes cellular mechanism evidence separately from randomized clinical efficacy.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Inhibits multiple receptor tyrosine kinases and fibroblast responses; slowing FVC decline does not isolate a single causal kinase pathway.

evidence.snippet: Frailty, pulmonary, or physical function were explored before and after intermittent D + Q; though under-powered to evaluate change, these measures do not appear to differ meaningfully between groups.
evidence.explanation: The randomized pilot supports feasibility, not clinical efficacy.

evidence.snippet: Sleep disturbances and anxiety were disproportionately represented in the D + Q arm (4/6 vs 0/6).
evidence.explanation: Adverse-event imbalance prevents an unqualified tolerability claim.

evidence.snippet: Physical function evaluated as 6-min walk distance, 4-m gait speed, and chair-stands time was significantly and clinically-meaningfully improved (p < .05). Pulmonary function, clinical chemistries, frailty index (FI-LAB), and reported health were unchanged.
evidence.explanation: Source for the uncontrolled 14-participant result described above. The split outcome is the point: physical function improved while pulmonary function did not, so an open-label study with no comparator supports feasibility and a systemic functional signal, not antifibrotic efficacy or senescent-cell target engagement in the IPF lung.

treatments/2.description: Investigational senolytic combination. An uncontrolled 14-participant study suggested physical-function changes without improved pulmonary function. A 12-participant randomized pilot demonstrated feasibility, with more nonserious adverse events on D+Q and no meaningful between-group functional difference. Neither study establishes antifibrotic efficacy or IPF-lung senescent-cell target engagement.

evidence.snippet: We show that the secretome of senescent fibroblasts, which are selectively killed by a senolytic cocktail, dasatinib plus quercetin (DQ), is fibrogenic.
evidence.explanation: Senolysis and a profibrotic secretome are demonstrated in fibroblasts; human IPF-lung target engagement remains unproven.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Targets senescent fibroblast survival in vitro; efficacy in patients remains investigational.

evidence.snippet: In patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, treatment with nerandomilast resulted in a smaller decline in the FVC than placebo over a period of 52 weeks.
evidence.explanation: FIBRONEER-IPF randomized 1177 participants, most on background antifibrotics; the endpoint supports slowing decline rather than reversal.

evidence.snippet: nerandomilast had no effect on the composite endpoint of time to first acute exacerbation of IPF, hospitalization for respiratory cause, or death
evidence.explanation: The final follow-up did not show benefit on this composite clinical endpoint.

treatments/3.description: Oral preferential PDE4B inhibitor approved for adult IPF. The phase III FIBRONEER-IPF trial showed less FVC decline at 52 weeks, with most participants receiving background nintedanib or pirfenidone. Diarrhea was common. Longer follow-up did not establish a reduction in the composite of acute exacerbation, respiratory hospitalization or death, so survival benefit is not asserted.

evidence.snippet: BI 1015550 inhibited transforming growth factor-β-stimulated myofibroblast transformation and the mRNA expression of various extracellular matrix proteins, as well as basic fibroblast growth factor plus interleukin-1β-induced cell proliferation.
evidence.explanation: Primary IPF fibroblast experiments support antiproliferative and differentiation effects; the 2023 corrigendum corrects Table 1 sample sizes without changing this conclusion.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Preferential PDE4B inhibition suppresses myofibroblast transformation and proliferation in primary IPF fibroblast cultures.

evidence.snippet: The recommendation for long-term oxygen therapy in patients with IPF and clinically significant resting hypoxemia is strong
evidence.explanation: The guideline supports this intervention in the indicated clinical setting.

treatments/4.description: Corrects clinically significant hypoxemia without reversing fibrosis.

evidence.explanation: The guideline supports this intervention in the indicated clinical setting.

evidence.snippet: Adjustment of immunosuppressive medication may be required to avoid drug toxicities in those w/hematologic abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Management guidance identifies a telomere-related transplant toxicity consideration rather than a blanket contraindication.

treatments/6.description: Consider transplantation for eligible patients with progressive disease. Telomere-related marrow, immune and liver complications influence assessment and immunosuppression.

evidence.explanation: The guideline supports this intervention in the indicated clinical setting.

treatments/6/targets/0.description: Consider transplantation for eligible patients with progressive disease. Telomere-related marrow, immune and liver complications influence assessment and immunosuppression.

evidence.snippet: Increased risks of death and hospitalization were observed in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis who were treated with a combination of prednisone, azathioprine, and NAC, as compared with placebo.
evidence.explanation: The randomized PANTHER-IPF result supports avoiding this regimen.

treatments/7.description: This chronic three-drug regimen should not be used to treat IPF. PANTHER-IPF found excess deaths and hospitalizations without physiological or clinical benefit. This result is specific to the regimen and does not establish that immune cells have no mechanistic role or address every acute-exacerbation treatment question.

evidence.snippet: Each child of an individual with a ... associated with predisposition to pulmonary fibrosis has a 50% chance of inheriting the pathogenic variant.
evidence.explanation: The recurrence statement applies to autosomal dominant monogenic predisposition, not every sporadic IPF case; inheritance of a variant does not predict age of onset or guarantee disease.

treatments/8.description: Offer specialist counseling when inherited pulmonary fibrosis is suspected or a pathogenic variant is identified. Discuss variable penetrance, possible anticipation and telomere inheritance, family evaluation and the distinction between variant transmission and disease prediction.

evidence.snippet: it has been suggested that repeated microinjuries of epithelial cells induce a wound healing response, during which fibroblasts differentiate into myofibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Supports the injury-centric model in which repetitive microinjury is the upstream initiating event that leads to fibroblast activation.

hypotheses/0.description: Repetitive alveolar epithelial injury is modeled as the primary upstream driver; AT2 cell senescence and subsequent fibroblast activation are downstream consequences of failed wound healing. Fibrosis represents an aberrant, non-resolving repair response to injury in genetically or environmentally susceptible individuals.

evidence.snippet: the autocrine TGF-β-positive feedback loop in AT2-lineage cells is a critical cellular system in non-inflammatory lung fibrogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Immune-cell-free organoids support an epithelial-fibroblast route in vitro, without proving whole-animal immune independence.

evidence.snippet: Loss of regenerative potential of alveolar type II epithelial cells (AT2) cells following injury has been postulated to underlie telomeropathy-associated lung fibrosis, with concomitant excessive proliferation of airway cells displaying abnormal phenotypes
evidence.explanation: Review describes telomere-driven loss of AT2 regenerative capacity as a mechanistic explanation for the strong age and telomere-length associations in IPF.

evidence.snippet: Meta-analysis of the two-sample mendelian randomisation results provided evidence inferring that shorter telomeres cause IPF
evidence.explanation: Published Mendelian randomization supports a contribution of shorter telomeres to IPF susceptibility under instrumental-variable assumptions. The COPD comparator does not establish disease specificity across all conditions or AT2-specific causal timing.

evidence.snippet: SPC-Tert cKO mice did not develop pulmonary fibrosis spontaneously up to 9 months of TERT deficiency. However, upon bleomycin treatment, they exhibited enhanced lung injury, inflammation, and fibrosis compared with control mice
evidence.explanation: AT2-specific TERT loss increases injury susceptibility and senescence without a significant change in AT2 telomere length. The absence of spontaneous fibrosis applies to this model only.

evidence.snippet: Pooled analysis showed shorter telomere length in IPF patients compared to controls (SMD: -0.84, 95%CI -1.21 to -0.48, Z = 4.55, p < 0.00001)
evidence.explanation: Observational pooled measurements support shorter telomeres in IPF. They complement genetic evidence but cannot alone establish causal ordering or an exclusive senescence-first subtype.

evidence.snippet: cGAS expression in fibrotic tissue from lungs of patients with IPF was detected within cells immunoreactive for epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) and p21, epithelial and senescence markers, respectively
evidence.explanation: Human colocalization supports pathway presence, while cultured-cell perturbations support cGAS-dependent senescence amplification. This does not establish universal STING activation or recruited immune-cell necessity.

evidence.snippet: mice with lung epithelial cell-specific deletion of CCL12 were protected from bleomycin-induced fibrosis
evidence.explanation: Epithelial CCL12 deletion limits macrophage recruitment and fibrosis in a specific bleomycin paradigm. Global deletion was not protective, and this is not a refutation of all epithelial-autonomous routes.

evidence.snippet: These results demonstrate that prolonged telomere dysfunction in type II AECs, but not collagen-expressing cells, leads to age-dependent lung remodeling and fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: Conditional TRF1 deletion causes spontaneous fibrosis after prolonged epithelial telomere dysfunction; this severe uncapping model is distinct from ordinary age-related shortening.

evidence.snippet: We used conditional loss of Sin3a in adult mouse AT2 cells to initiate a program of p53-dependent cellular senescence, AT2 cell depletion, and spontaneous, progressive pulmonary fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: An AT2-directed genetic perturbation produces spontaneous progressive fibrosis without bleomycin; it does not establish immune independence or the initiating lesion in all human IPF.

hypotheses/1.description: AT2 senescence and loss of regenerative capacity may be proximal drivers of fibrosis, particularly in telomere-associated disease but also after other stress pathways. Human genetics and tissue studies support relevance; TRF1 and Sin3a mouse perturbations demonstrate spontaneous fibrosis, whereas other telomerase models require injury. Immune-cell-free organoids establish one epithelial-fibroblast route. The relative contributions of this route and immune amplification in human disease remain unresolved.

evidence.snippet: The pathogenesis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) involves a complex interplay of cell types and signaling pathways. Recurrent alveolar epithelial cell (AEC) injury may occur in the context of predisposing factors (e.g., genetic, environmental, epigenetic, immunologic, and gerontologic), leading to metabolic dysfunction, senescence, aberrant epithelial cell activation, and dysregulated epithelial repair.
evidence.explanation: Annual Review of Pathology review frames IPF as a convergence of multiple predisposing factors and cell types, consistent with the feedback loop model in which no single upstream event fully explains the disease.

hypotheses/2.description: Epithelial stress, senescence, fibroblast persistence and matrix-derived mechanical signals may reinforce one another after initiation. Experimental TGF-beta and matrix-stiffness feedback support this convergent framework, but their relative necessity and therapeutic importance in human IPF remain unresolved.

evidence.snippet: These results demonstrate that prolonged telomere dysfunction in type II AECs, but not collagen-expressing cells, leads to age-dependent lung remodeling and fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: Conditional TRF1 deletion causes spontaneous fibrosis after prolonged epithelial telomere dysfunction; this severe uncapping model is distinct from ordinary age-related shortening.

evidence.snippet: We used conditional loss of Sin3a in adult mouse AT2 cells to initiate a program of p53-dependent cellular senescence, AT2 cell depletion, and spontaneous, progressive pulmonary fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: An AT2-directed genetic perturbation produces spontaneous progressive fibrosis without bleomycin; it does not establish immune independence or the initiating lesion in all human IPF.

open_questions/0.rationale: Human disease likely combines epithelial susceptibility, injury and failed repair. TRF1 and Sin3a perturbations demonstrate spontaneous fibrosis in mice, while AT2-specific TERT loss and certain surfactant variants require additional injury. The unresolved question is how these distinct model-specific mechanisms map onto human causal ordering, not whether any spontaneous model exists.

open_questions/1.rationale: Autocrine TGF-beta, matrix mechanics and persistent mesenchymal states can sustain experimental fibrosis. Human relative contributions and optimal combinations of interventions remain unresolved. Antifibrotic therapies slow FVC decline but do not establish reversal, while senolytic clinical studies remain small feasibility trials.

open_questions/2.rationale: The reviewed evidence combines clinical associations and preclinical gut-lung experiments. Directionality, specific microbial mediators, and independence from disease severity, diet and drug exposure remain unresolved. Human microbiome-directed therapeutic benefit is not established by the cited review.

open_questions/3.rationale: The rs35705950 promoter variant is the strongest common genetic risk factor for sporadic IPF, and Hancock et al. report MUC5B co-expression with surfactant protein C in type 2 alveolar epithelium and in honeycomb-cyst epithelium (PMID:30560893), which places it in the same cells this entry models as senescent. The mechanism it is curated under, impaired distal mucociliary clearance, is not a senescence mechanism, and no study has asked whether MUC5B overexpression induces, protects against, or is orthogonal to AT2 senescence. If the two mechanisms are independent, risk should be close to additive and the mucociliary and senescence routes would describe partly different patients; if they interact, departure from additivity is expected. An OpenScientist report of the senescence-first model records PubMed searches for MUC5B with senescence and with telomere that returned no relevant studies, but commits no query log, so this is a reported absence rather than a documented one.

evidence.snippet: IgA pemphigus is characterized by tissue-bound and circulating IgA antibodies targeting desmosomal or nondesmosomal cell surface components in the epidermis.
evidence.explanation: The defining immunopathology. Graded OTHER because it is a review's definitional statement.

evidence.snippet: Daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (DLd) therapy was effective for both the MM and the skin lesions, resulting in negative results on Dsg1/3 and Dsc1-3 IgA ELISAs.
evidence.explanation: Treating the plasma-cell clone abolished both the disease and the autoantibody, which is the closest thing in this literature to a demonstration that the clone is the source.

steps/0.description:
The initiating event, and the one that defines the disease: production of IgA autoantibodies binding the keratinocyte cell surface. The isotype is the diagnostic criterion - IgA pemphigus is defined by tissue-bound and circulating IgA antibodies where the other three pemphigus variants are defined by IgG.
What triggers the autoantibody response is not known. The association with IgA monoclonal gammopathy (9.5 percent of reported patients) and with IgA multiple myeloma is the strongest clue available, and in the myeloma cases the antibody titre tracks the plasma-cell clone: treating the myeloma with daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone cleared both the skin lesions and the anti-desmoglein and anti-desmocollin IgA ELISAs.

evidence.snippet: Intercellular deposition of IgA was noted in almost all patients (97.0%), and the remaining 3.0% of patients had IgA positivity on indirect immunofluorescence or enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay confirming the diagnosis.
evidence.explanation: The frequency of the defining tissue finding, across 137 patients.

evidence.snippet: IgA circulating intercellular antibodies were detected in only 66.7% patients.
evidence.explanation: The serum-versus-tissue discrepancy, which is why direct immunofluorescence rather than serology is the primary test.

steps/1.description:
Bound IgA in the intercellular space between keratinocytes, demonstrable by direct immunofluorescence in essentially every patient - 97 percent of the systematic review's cohort, with the remaining 3 percent diagnosed on indirect immunofluorescence or ELISA instead.
The level at which it deposits is what separates the subtypes: the upper epidermis in the SPD type, the entire epidermis in the IEN type. Note the asymmetry with circulating antibody - only 66.7 percent of patients had detectable circulating IgA intercellular antibodies, so a negative serum does not exclude the disease and biopsy with direct immunofluorescence is the test that matters.

evidence.snippet: The cross-linking of the IgA Fc receptor (FcαRI) by IgA induces release of the chemoattractant LTB4, thereby recruiting neutrophils in a positive feedback loop. IgA autoantibodies of patients with autoimmune blistering skin diseases therefore induce massive recruitment of neutrophils, resulting in severe tissue damage.
evidence.explanation: The mechanism and its application to IgA-mediated blistering disease, in one sentence pair. This is the step the entry previously asserted only in prose.

evidence.snippet: Cross‐linking of FcαRI by IgA‐immune complexes initiates robust inflammatory responses, including superoxide production, release of cytokines, phagocytosis, antigen presentation and release of neutrophil extracellular traps
evidence.explanation: The effector repertoire the receptor triggers. Note the source uses non-breaking hyphens, reproduced exactly as cached.

evidence.snippet: IgA can also be involved in disease pathology, because it provides a potent stimulus to activate neutrophils after crosslinking of surface CD89 (FcaRI), resulting in chronic inflammation and tissue damage
evidence.explanation: The receptor's pro-inflammatory role restated in the context of a therapeutic-antagonism programme. Not independent corroboration: van Egmond is senior author on this paper and on the one quoted above, both from the same VU Amsterdam anti-CD89 programme, and the quoted sentence is this paper's introduction citing its own group's prior work. That matters here, because this node is graded ESTABLISHED on evidence that is admittedly not disease-specific, so how much independent corroboration it carries is load-bearing.

steps/2.description:
The step that makes the isotype matter, and the reason this disease is neutrophilic where the IgG pemphigus variants are not. FcalphaRI (CD89) is the IgA Fc receptor, expressed on neutrophils, eosinophils, monocytes and several macrophage subsets. Cross-linking it with IgA immune complexes sets off superoxide production, cytokine release, phagocytosis, degranulation and NET release - and, critically, release of the chemoattractant leukotriene B4, which recruits further neutrophils in a positive feedback loop.
That loop is useful against IgA-opsonised bacteria, where it self-terminates when the organism is cleared. Against a fixed autoantigen in the epidermis it does not terminate, which is the account this entry curates of why the inflammation is sustained.
The evidence is not disease-specific to IgA pemphigus: it is receptor biology, established in human neutrophils and in a linear IgA bullous disease mouse model, and applied here to a disease that shares the isotype and the neutrophil-rich histology. That is stated rather than glossed, because the node is graded ESTABLISHED on the strength of the receptor work rather than on any IgA pemphigus experiment.

evidence.snippet: These results convincingly indicate that human Dsc1 is an autoantigen for SPD-type IgA pemphigus, suggesting the possibility of an important role for Dsc1 in the pathogenesis of this disease.
evidence.explanation: The antigen identification. Note the authors' own hedge - "suggesting the possibility of an important role" - which is why this node is PROVISIONAL.

evidence.snippet: However, except for the findings of a few in vitro and in vivo studies, there is currently no clear evidence for the pathogenicity of anti-Dsc autoantibodies in pemphigus, whereas significance of anti-Dsg autoantibodies is well established.
evidence.explanation: The explicit statement that the pathogenic step is unproven. Graded PARTIAL because it qualifies rather than supports the causal claim.

steps/3.description:
In SPD-type disease the antibody's target is desmocollin 1, a desmosomal cadherin that with the desmogleins holds keratinocytes together, so the expected consequence is loss of intercellular adhesion. That expectation is the standard account of the disease and it is what makes it a pemphigus.
Graded PROVISIONAL deliberately, because the pathogenicity of anti-desmocollin autoantibodies is not established the way anti-desmoglein pathogenicity is. A 2023 review of the question puts it plainly: beyond a few in vitro and in vivo studies there is currently no clear evidence that anti-Dsc autoantibodies are pathogenic, in contrast to the well-established significance of the anti-Dsg ones. The antigen is identified; the causal step from binding it to blistering is inferred.

evidence.snippet: Histopathologically, slight epidermal acantholysis and extensive neutrophilic infiltration in either the upper part or all layers of the epidermis were observed.
evidence.explanation: The histological pattern and the relative weight of its two components. Graded OTHER because it is a review's synthesis across reported cases.

evidence.snippet: Histopathology showed intraepidermal blisters or pustules at the upper epidermis in the SPD-type and at the midepidermis in the IEN-type.
evidence.explanation: The level of the epidermis involved in each subtype, in 29 classified cases.

steps/4.description:
The step that makes this disease pustular rather than bullous, and the one that follows from the isotype. Histology shows extensive neutrophilic infiltration of the epidermis - confined to the upper part in the SPD type, through all layers in the IEN type - with the acantholysis, where present, slight.
That inversion of emphasis relative to IgG pemphigus is the mechanistic signature: in pemphigus vulgaris the acantholysis is the lesion and neutrophils are incidental, here the neutrophils are the lesion and the acantholysis is a minor finding.

evidence.snippet: there are IgA autoantibodies targeting the keratinocyte cell surface adhesion molecules, causing cell-to-cell dehiscence and a flaccid vesiculopustular eruption, mainly in the axilla and groin
evidence.explanation: The full chain from antibody to lesion and its distribution. Graded OTHER because it is the case report's background framing.

steps/5.description: The lesion. Neutrophil accumulation with slight acantholysis produces intraepidermal pustules and vesicles, which clinically appear as flaccid vesiculopustules on annular or circinate erythematous plaques, characteristically in the axillae and groin but capable of involving the whole trunk and scalp.

evidence.snippet: Most patients presented with vesicles (80.8%), pustules (75.0%), and circinate plaques (63.6%).
evidence.explanation: Frequencies of the three cardinal lesions across 137 reported patients.

steps/6.description: Flaccid vesicles, the commonest reported lesion at 80.8 percent of patients in the systematic review.

evidence.snippet: Most patients presented with vesicles (80.8%), pustules (75.0%), and circinate plaques (63.6%).
evidence.explanation: Pustule frequency in the pooled cohort.

steps/7.description: Sterile pustules, present in three-quarters of reported patients. Their prominence, relative to the frank bullae of IgG pemphigus, is the clinical expression of the neutrophil-dominant mechanism.

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of IgA pemphigus may be considered in patients presenting with vesiculopustular eruption and circinate plaques with truncal and extremity involvement.
evidence.explanation: The review's own diagnostic recommendation, which is what marks this phenotype as diagnostic.

steps/8.description: Ring-shaped or arcuate erythematous plaques with vesicles and pustules at the advancing edge, in about two-thirds of patients. Together with the vesiculopustular eruption this is the presentation the systematic review proposes should raise the diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: Pruritus was present in 65.6% of reported patients.
evidence.explanation: Itch frequency in the pooled cohort.

steps/9.description: Itch, reported in about two-thirds of patients and prominent enough that the eruption is routinely described as pruritic. It is a substantive part of the disease burden rather than an incidental symptom, since the skin lesions themselves are rarely life-threatening.

evidence.snippet: extensive neutrophilic infiltration in either the upper part or all layers of the epidermis were observed
evidence.explanation: The histological hallmark. Graded OTHER because it is a review's synthesis.

steps/10.description: The defining histological finding: neutrophils within the epidermis, upper layers in SPD type and mid or full thickness in IEN type.

evidence.snippet: Histopathology showed subcorneal pustules containing a few acantholytic cells
evidence.explanation: Acantholysis present but sparse, in a well-characterised SPD-type case.

evidence.snippet: Acantholysis of keratinocytes is not a feature of IgA pemphigus, unlike pemphigus vulgaris.
evidence.explanation: Directly contradicts the phenotype as curated, and kept rather than omitted because the fact that a 2024 case report makes the claim is itself evidence that the point is unsettled in this literature. Two other cited sources describe acantholytic cells and one describes acantholytic blisters, so the flat denial is not supportable on its own. NO_EVIDENCE is deliberate and is the weakest part of this item. REFUTE would read better as direction, but on a phenotypes[] item it is also a publication decision: it maps to an HPOA NOT qualifier, so it would assert to downstream consumers that IgA pemphigus does not feature acantholysis - a claim this very explanation argues against. Grading it SUPPORT is worse still, and is what the retired WRONG_STATEMENT value silently did here. NO_EVIDENCE publishes nothing while leaving the source, the quote and this reasoning visible. The substantive disagreement is carried by the phenotype description and by discussions[1].

steps/11.description:
Loss of keratinocyte cohesion. It is present but slight - reviews describe a few acantholytic cells within the pustules - and one case report states outright that acantholysis is not a feature of IgA pemphigus, unlike pemphigus vulgaris.
Curated as OCCASIONAL and flagged in a discussion rather than smoothed over, because the sources genuinely disagree about whether it is present at all, and because that disagreement bears directly on whether the desmocollin antibody is doing what the disease name implies.

edges/5.description: The edge that carries this entry's central uncertainty into the graph. If anti-desmocollin IgA is pathogenic, this is how acantholysis arises; the node it leaves is graded PROVISIONAL for exactly that reason, and the phenotype it reaches is curated OCCASIONAL with a source that denies it occurs at all.

evidence.snippet: Oral dapsone and corticosteroids were the mostly commonly used treatments.
evidence.explanation: Established practice across the whole reported literature. The typo is the source's.

evidence.snippet: Dapsone, despite being the drug of choice for treating IgA pemphigus, is not effective in clearing lesions in a minority of patients
evidence.explanation: Establishes both the first-line status and its failure rate. Graded PARTIAL because it qualifies the treatment as much as it supports it.

treatments/0.description:
The drug of choice, and mechanistically apt: dapsone's anti-inflammatory action is on neutrophil function, which is the effector arm of this disease rather than an incidental feature of it. Oral dapsone and corticosteroids were the two commonest treatments across the entire reported literature.
It is not reliably effective. A minority of patients do not clear on it, and recalcitrant disease is well enough recognised to have a second-line list - colchicine, sulfapyridine, acitretin - and reported failures even of those.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Dapsone suppresses neutrophil recruitment and function, which is the effector step in this disease. It does not act on the autoantibody.

evidence.snippet: Oral dapsone and corticosteroids were the mostly commonly used treatments.
evidence.explanation: Corticosteroids as one of the two commonest treatments in the pooled literature.

treatments/1.description: The other commonly used first-line agent, usually alongside dapsone. The reported evidence is practice rather than trial: no controlled comparison of any treatment in this disease exists.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Broad suppression of the inflammatory infiltrate, without specificity for the autoantibody or its target.

evidence.snippet: Combined therapy with dapsone and etretinate improved the skin lesions.
evidence.explanation: A retinoid-containing regimen working in an SPD-type case.

evidence.snippet: Systemic treatment with isotretinoin 25 mg/d and prednisone 20 mg/d achieved only a slight effect after six months.
evidence.explanation: A retinoid failing, with dose and duration. Graded REFUTE because it is evidence against retinoid efficacy in this patient rather than qualified support for it.

treatments/2.description: Retinoids appear in this literature in two guises and it is worth keeping them apart. Etretinate combined with dapsone improved a well-characterised SPD-type case, and acitretin is on the standard recalcitrant-disease list. But isotretinoin at 25 mg daily with prednisone achieved only a slight effect after six months in a reported IEN-type case with anti-desmoglein IgA - so the class is not uniformly useful, and the one clear failure was in the subtype whose antigen is unknown.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report the successful treatment of a 50-year-old male patient with an adalimumab injection who had a poor response to dapsone.
evidence.explanation: The single reported case, with the response and the prior failure both stated.

treatments/3.description: Reported once, for dapsone-recalcitrant disease: a 50-year-old man who had responded poorly to dapsone cleared on adalimumab. A single case, so it is curated as an option of last resort rather than an established second line - but it is mechanistically coherent, since TNF-alpha blockade suppresses the neutrophilic inflammation that drives the lesions.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: TNF-alpha blockade reduces neutrophil recruitment into the epidermis.

evidence.snippet: Daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (DLd) therapy was effective for both the MM and the skin lesions, resulting in negative results on Dsg1/3 and Dsc1-3 IgA ELISAs.
evidence.explanation: Clinical and serological response of the skin disease to myeloma-directed therapy.

treatments/4.description:
Where an IgA myeloma is present, treating it treats the skin. In the reported case daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone cleared both the lesions and the anti-desmoglein and anti-desmocollin IgA ELISAs.
This is the only reported treatment that acts on the autoantibody's source rather than on the downstream inflammation, which is why it is curated separately from the immunosuppressants. It applies to a small minority.
therapeutic_modality is OTHER rather than MONOCLONAL_ANTIBODY: daratumumab is one of three components, and the regimen as given also contains an immunomodulatory small molecule and a corticosteroid. Tagging the whole regimen by its antibody component would misclassify it. All three agents are bound individually instead.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: Eliminating the IgA-secreting plasma cell clone removes the source of the autoantibody, which is upstream of every other treatment in this entry.

open_questions/0.rationale:
This entry uses the conventional two subtypes, and it should be read as a working scheme rather than a settled nosology.
The pressure on it is from published cases: IgA reactive with all three desmocollins in an SPD-type patient; IgA to desmogleins 1 and 3 in an IEN-type patient; IgA to desmocollins 2 and 3 together with BP180. The largest cohort could not classify eight of forty-nine cases at all and found subgroups it had to call IgA-pemphigus vegetans, foliaceus and vulgaris. One review, tallying its own case against twenty prior atypical reports, concluded the classification schemes are limited and proposed replacing them with a general "IGAP spectrum".
The reason not to act on that yet is that the two-type scheme is doing real work: it separates the one subtype with a known antigen from the one without, and the antigen difference is the only hard biological distinction available. A spectrum model would dissolve that. Recorded here so the decision is visible and revisitable rather than implied by the file's structure.

open_questions/1.rationale:
Desmocollin 1 is securely established as the SPD-type autoantigen - the transfection experiment is clean, with six of six SPD sera binding Dsc1 and none binding Dsc2 or Dsc3. What is not established is that binding it causes the disease. A 2023 review of exactly this question concludes that beyond a few in vitro and in vivo studies there is no clear evidence for the pathogenicity of anti-desmocollin autoantibodies, in contrast to the well-established significance of anti-desmoglein antibodies.
The histology points the same way. Acantholysis - the thing an adhesion-molecule antibody should produce - is slight where it is present at all, and one 2024 case report states flatly that it is not a feature of the disease. The dominant finding is neutrophilic. So an alternative reading is available and is not excluded by anything cited here: that the IgA acts mainly by recruiting neutrophils, and that the adhesion molecule it happens to bind is a marker of the disease rather than its mechanism.
This is why the adhesion node is graded PROVISIONAL while the neutrophil node is ESTABLISHED, and why the acantholysis phenotype keeps the source that disagrees as a NO_EVIDENCE item rather than dropping it.

evidence.snippet: The mutations disrupted protein stability by interfering with homodimerization or by causing aggregation.
evidence.explanation: States the molecular consequence of the variants directly, and is the reason this entry records LOSS_OF_FUNCTION rather than DOMINANT_NEGATIVE.

evidence.snippet: Reduced BACH2 expression and deficient transcriptional repression of the BACH2 target, BLIMP1, were detected in PBMCs or lymphoblastoid cell lines of our patient.
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation in a second family that a BRIDA variant lowers BACH2 protein and its repressor output, in patient-derived cells.
